rules.title: Unnecessary async/await usage
rules.desc: When a method only awaits a single expression as its last statement and returns the result, the async/await keywords add unnecessary overhead. Return the Task directly and let the caller await it. This reduces state machine allocation and improves performance. Exception: Keep async/await when you need try/catch around the await or when the method has multiple awaits.

rules.title: Long running / blocking operations under an async method
Blocking call inside an async method
rules.desc: Blocking calls like Task.Result, Task.Wait(), Thread.Sleep(), or Task.GetAwaiter().GetResult() inside async methods can cause deadlocks, especially in UI or ASP.NET contexts with synchronization contexts. Use the async equivalents: await instead of .Result/.Wait(), Task.Delay() instead of Thread.Sleep(), Task.WhenAll() instead of Task.WaitAll().

rules.title: Avoid fire & forget async methods
Fire-and-forget async-void methods or delegates
rules.desc: Async void methods cannot be awaited, making it impossible to know when they complete or to catch their exceptions. Exceptions thrown in async void methods will crash the process. Use 'async Task' instead, which allows proper exception handling and await support. The only valid use case for async void is event handlers.

rules.title: Fire-and-forget async call inside a using block
rules.desc: When an async method is called without await inside a using block, the disposable resource may be disposed before the async operation completes, causing exceptions or undefined behavior. Always await async calls that depend on resources in the using scope.

rules.title: Nested Task<Task> from TaskFactory.StartNew with async lambda
rules.desc: Using TaskFactory.StartNew() with an async lambda creates a Task<Task> (nested task). Awaiting only the outer task doesn't wait for the inner async operation to complete. Use Task.Run() instead, which automatically unwraps async lambdas, or call .Unwrap() on the result.

rules.title: Task<T> to Task conversion silently discards result
rules.desc: A non-async lambda returning Task<T> is being assigned to a delegate expecting Task (e.g., Func<Task>). The result value is silently discarded due to implicit conversion from Task<T> to Task. Unlike async lambdas which produce compiler error CS8031 for this pattern, non-async lambdas compile without warning. Either change the delegate type to Func<Task<T>> to preserve the result, or explicitly discard it if intentional.

rules.title: Use lock files
rules.desc: By default, the package versions specified by either the PackageReference or PackageVersion are used as constraints for which dependency versions are allowed to be used when building the project. This means that the resolved package versions might change over time, leading to non-reproducible builds or security issues. In order to prevent these issues, it is advisable to enable .NET's lock files when building your production code. This requires setting the RestorePackagesWithLockFile property to true, and ensuring that locked mode is enabled when building for production.

rules.title: Enable <RestoreLockedMode> when <ContinuousIntegrationBuild> is enabled
rules.desc: In order to ensure dotnet restore is not allowed to implicitly upgrade package versions that are specified in the lock file. It is necessary to enable "locked mode". The recommended way of enabling locked mode is to conditionally set the RestoreLockedMode property to true, if the ContinuousIntegrationBuild is set to true. This is under the assumption that there is a dynamic way in place that ensures ContinuousIntegrationBuild is set to true in CI pipelines.

rules.title: Convention-based MSBuild file names should use correct casing
rules.desc: Some MSBuild files have a certain role during the build based on a naming convention. Although MSBuild is mostly case-insensitive, having different casing might cause issues.

rules.title: Update statements should change state

rules.title: Prefer attributes over elements

rules.title: Run analyzers during build

rules.title: Generate documentation file
rules.desc: In order for code documentation to be visible for package consumers it is important that the documentation is generated.

rules.title: Don't mix Version and VersionPrefix/VersionSuffix
rules.desc: Version node overrides VersionPrefix and VersionSuffix nodes , therefore you should either remove the Version node (if you want to use the VersionPrefix and VersionSuffix nodes) or you should remove the VersionPrefix and VersionSuffix nodes (if you want to use Version node).

rules.title: Define VersionPrefix if VersionSuffix is defined
rules.desc: VersionSuffix indicates the desire to use the VersionPrefix and VersionSuffix system , but when only defining the VersionSuffix node, the default value of VersionPrefix (1.0.0) is used, which is most likely an error.

rules.title: Enable strict mode for package baseline validation
rules.desc: When ensuring backwards compatibility of the API surface of your package, it is advised to do this in strict mode. This helps preventing any unintentional API changes.

rules.title: Enable strict mode for package runtime compatibility validation
rules.desc: When building your package for multiple runtimes it is advised to enable the strict mode of the runtime compatibility validation.

rules.title: Enable strict mode for package framework compatibility validation
rules.desc: When building your package for multiple runtimes it is advised to enable the strict mode of the framework compatibility validation.

rules.title: Generate API compatibility suppression file
rules.desc: This suppression file can be created manually, or automatically generated by enabling the `GenerateCompatibilitySuppressionFile` property.It is advised to enable this property in the project file to ensure that file is kept up-to-date automatically.

rules.title: Enable API compatibility attribute checks
rules.desc: When package validation is enabled, it is advised to opt-in to the strict attribute compatibility checks.

rules.title: Enable API compatibility parameter name checks
rules.desc: When package validation is enabled, it is advised to opt-in to the strict parameter name compatibility checks.

rules.title: Versions should be compliant with Semantic Versioning
rules.desc: Versions should comply with Semantic Versioning to help clarifying the meaning of the (code) changes made.

rules.title: Version prefixes should be compliant with Semantic Versioning
rules.desc: Versions should comply with Semantic Versioning to help clarifying the meaning of the (code) changes made.

rules.title: Configure NuGet explicitly
rules.desc: The only way to ensure that NuGet is setup safely is by adding a NuGet.config file that is part of the source code.

rules.title: Clear previously defined package sources
rules.desc: To prevent supply chain attacks no package sources should be inherited from globally defined sources that could contain malicious sources.

rules.title: NuGet authentication should be secure
rules.desc: NuGet authentication should use secure, externalized credentials. Storing credentials securely prevents accidental exposure in source control and reduces the risk of unauthorized access.

rules.title: Define a mapping for each package source
rules.desc: To prevent supply chain attacks each <packageSource> should have its own <packageSourceMapping>. By doing so, the origin of packages is predictable.

rules.title: Package source mappings should be unique
rules.desc: The first package source mapping that matches serves the package. Therefore, a second mapping with the same pattern will never match.

rules.title: Last source map should map all packages
rules.desc: Mappings are evaluated from top to bottom, the first matching mapping is used. To ensure all packages can be served by at least one package, the last one should be a match all (*).

rules.title: Avoid local package sources
rules.desc: Package sources should be verifiable and reliable. A local package source is most likely neither of those.

rules.title: Define the project publishability explicitly
rules.desc: To prevent confusion, explicitly define the <IsPublishable> node.

rules.title: Only publish executables
rules.desc: Running dotnet publish on projects other than executables will not publish anything and is considered a mistake.

rules.title: Test projects should not be packable
rules.desc: Test projects should only be responsible for running tests. Hence they should not be packable.

rules.title: Test projects should not be publishable
rules.desc: Test projects should only be responsible for running tests. Hence they should not be publishable.

rules.title: Test projects require Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk
rules.desc: Tests in a test projects do not run properly without the Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk being included.

rules.title: Using Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk implies a test project
rules.desc: Including the Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk is only useful for test projects.

rules.title: Only include packages with an explicitly defined license
rules.desc: To prevent legal issues, do not rely on third-party references that do not come with an explicitly defined license.

rules.title: Package only contains a deprecated license URL
rules.desc: To prevent legal issues, do not rely on third-party references that do not come with a verifiable and not deprecated license URL.

rules.title: Only include packages compliant with project
rules.desc: To prevent legal issues do not rely on third-party references with a custom defined license that has not been manually reviewed.

rules.title: Package license is unknown
rules.desc: To prevent legal issues do not rely on third-party references with a custom defined license that has not been manually reviewed.

rules.title: Package license has changed
rules.desc: To prevent legal issues do not rely on third-party references where the license has been changed without checking the changes.

rules.title: Third-party license registry requires include
rules.desc: To prevent legal issues do not rely on third-party references where the license has been changed without checking the changes.

rules.title: Third-party license registry requires hash
rules.desc: To prevent legal issues do not rely on third-party references where the license has been changed without checking the changes.

rules.title: Third-party license registry must be unconditional
rules.desc: To prevent legal issues do not rely on third-party references where the license has been changed without checking the changes.

rules.title: Order third-party licenses alphabetically
rules.desc: Not ordering third-party licenses alphabetically is considered noise.

rules.title: NuGet package cache could not be resolved
rules.desc: The rules that check for licenses need (read) access to the package cache. If that location could not be resolved, none of those rules work properly.

rules.title: Avoid generating packages on build if not packable
rules.desc: The <GeneratePackageOnBuild> option has no effect when the <IsPackable> node is disabled. Removing the <GeneratePackageOnBuild> node will reduce noise.

rules.title: Avoid defining <Compile> items in SDK project
rules.desc: The .net.csproj SDK project is a placeholder for non-compiling files. Compile items should be avoided.

rules.title: Configure Central Package Management explicitly
rules.desc: In situations where you manage common dependencies for many different projects, you can leverage Central Package Version Management (CPM) features to do all of this from a single location.

rules.title: Include 'Directory.Packages.props'
rules.desc: When CPM is enabled 'Directory.Packages.props' should be resolvable.

rules.title: Enable Central Package Management centrally
rules.desc: Enabling it per project would defy the purpose of CPM.

rules.title: Use VersionOverride only with Central Package Management enabled
rules.desc: When CPM is not enabled the use of <PackageReference VersionOverride /> `has no effect, and is most likely a mistake.

rules.title: Use Version only with Central Package Management not enabled
rules.desc: When CPM is enabled the use of <PackageReference Version /> `has no effect, and is most likely a mistake.

rules.title: Define version for PackageReference
rules.desc: PackageReference nodes require a version number in order to properly resolve the package. This can be done by either using the Version attribute on the PackageReference node, or by using a matching PackageVersion node.

rules.title: VersionOverride should change the version
rules.desc: The use of VersionOverride on a <PackageReference> is only useful when it defines a different version than already defined by the CPM.

rules.title: Only use Directory.Packages.props for Central Package Management
rules.desc: The use of VersionOverride on a <PackageReference> is only useful when it defines a different version than already defined by the CPM.

rules.title: Define CPM related configuration only in Directory.Packages.props
rules.desc: The use of <GlobalPackageReference> is only useful when defined in Directory.Packages.props.

rules.title: Global package references are meant for private assets only
rules.desc: When using <GlobalPackageReference>, the reference is included as private asset. Packages not meant as private asset should not be included via a global package reference.

rules.title: Remove unused package versions
rules.desc: Keeping a package version for a package that is not used is adding noise to the Directory.Packages.props file.

rules.title: Directory.Build.props and Directory.Packages.props should be in the same directory
rules.desc: To prevent confusion, the Directory.Build.props and Directory.Packages.props imported by a MS build project file, should be in the same directory.

rules.title: Remove redundant packages references that are globally referenced
rules.desc: Importing packages twice is only adding noise.

rules.title: Global package references only work when CPM is enabled
rules.desc: To benefit from <GlobalPackageReference>'s, CPM has to be enabled.

rules.title: Use the .NET project file analyzers
rules.desc: To improve the code quality of .NET project files.

rules.title: Use analyzers for packages
rules.desc: Some NuGet packages come with their own/dedicated Roslyn analyzers; they just contain rules to improve the usage of those packages. In order to get the best out of those NuGet packages, their analyzer(s) should be used.

rules.title: Use Microsoft's .NET analyzers
rules.desc: Improve the code quality by adding Microsoft's Roslyn analyzers.

rules.title: Use Sonar analyzers for packages
rules.desc: Improve the code quality by adding Sonar's Roslyn analyzers.

rules.title: Suppress NuGet issues per package
rules.desc: As the raised issues are reported on a specific dependency, it is best to suppress it on that specific dependency only (assuming it is safe to do so).

rules.title: Suppress NuGet advisories per vulnerability
rules.desc: As the raised advisories are reported on a specific vulnerability, it is best to suppress it on that specific vulnerability only (assuming it is safe to do so) using <NuGetAuditSuppress>.

rules.title: Avoid using Moq
rules.desc: Moq has built in data harvesting that violates GDPR.

rules.title: Package references should have stable versions
rules.desc: The use of nightly builds and other pre-releases should be avoided.

rules.title: Use Coverlet Collector or MSBuild
rules.desc: The packages coverlet.collector and coverlet.msbuild have the same purpose but should not be used together.

rules.title: TUnit test projects must be executable
rules.desc: TUnit builds upon the Microsoft.Testing.Platform which requires the project to be an executable.

rules.title: TUnit conflicts with Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk
rules.desc: The use of the Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk interferes with the working of TUnit, therefore they can not be combined.

rules.title: Exclude private assets as project file dependency
rules.desc: Private assets (such as analyzers) will not result in being a project dependency after being compiled.

rules.title: Avoid project references to executables
rules.desc: Executables should not be referenced by other projects

rules.title: Project references to packable targets should be packable
rules.desc: Packable projects should only reference packable projects

rules.title: Avoid project references to test projects
rules.desc: Test projects should not be referenced by other projects

rules.title: Avoid project references to benchmark projects
rules.desc: Benchmark projects should not be referenced by other projects

rules.title: Indent XML files
rules.desc: To improve readability, XML elements should be properly indented.

rules.title: Use <![CDATA[ for large texts
rules.desc: To improve readability, large texts should be CDATA.

rules.title: Omit XML declarations
rules.desc: The XML declaration is redundant for MS Build project files.

rules.title: MSBuild child elements should be separated by an empty line
rules.desc: To improve readability, MSBuild child elements should be separated by empty lines.

rules.title: Embed valid resource files
rules.desc: A resource file should contain valid XML.

rules.title: Define data in a resource file
rules.desc: A resource file without `<data>` elements is of no use.

rules.title: Sort resource file values alphabetically
rules.desc: To improve readability, and reduce the number of merge conflicts, the `<data>` elements should be sorted based on the `@name` attribute.

rules.title: Add invariant fallback resources
rules.desc: To ensure that localized values can be resolved, a localized resource file must have a culture invariant alternative.

rules.title: Add invariant fallback values
rules.desc: To ensure that localized values can be resolved, a localized value file must have a culture invariant alternative.

rules.title: Escape XML nodes of resource values
rules.desc: To ensure correct handling, XML nodes within resource values should be escaped.

rules.title: Indent XML files
rules.desc: To improve readability, XML elements should be properly indented.

rules.title: Only use UTF-8 encoding without BOM
rules.desc: The use of BOM for UTF-8 can cause systems to malfunction. This includes multiple web based files such as Javascript and CSS.

rules.title: Track uses of "TODO" tags
rules.desc: Developers often use TODO tags to mark areas in the code where additional work or improvements are needed but are not implemented immediately.

rules.title: Remove commented-out code
rules.desc: Commented-out code adds noise to a file and makes it harder to follow the code that should be executed.

rules.title: Trim whitespace
rules.desc: Leading or trailing insignificant whitespace can cause syntax errors or make the comparing of file changes harder.

rules.title: Invalid INI file
rules.desc: A part of the INI file could not be parsed.

rules.title: Invalid INI Header
rules.desc: An INI header should have the format [<Header>].

rules.title: Invalid INI key-value pair
rules.desc: An INI key-value pair should have the format <Key> ( : | = ) <Value>.

rules.title: Sections should contain at least one key-value pair
rules.desc: A Section in INI file groups key-value pairs. Having an empty section has no added value.

rules.title: Define INI key once
rules.desc: Within sections of an INI file, setting a key more than once will result in overriding the current value and is considered a mistake.

rules.title: Remove section header
rules.desc: A .globalconfig file strictly requires all key-value to sit at the root level; any section headers or glob patterns inside the file are ignored by the Roslyn compiler.

rules.title: Specify is_global
rules.desc: By explicitly setting is_global = true, the settings are correctly applied globally across the entire project or solution, even if the file uses a custom name instead of .globalconfig.

rules.title: Use valid diagnostic severity value
rules.desc: The compiler requires standard severity keywords to parse .globalconfig files. Using invalid values prevents the rule from being applied as intended.

rules.title: Use explicit diagnostic severity level
rules.desc: By explicitly setting is_global = true, the settings are correctly applied globally across the entire project or solution, even if the file uses a custom name instead of .globalconfig.

rules.title: Use valid diagnostic severity value
rules.desc: The compiler requires standard severity keywords to parse .globalconfig files. Using invalid values prevents the rule from being applied as intended.

rules.title: Avoid global diagnostic suppression
rules.desc: Disabling all diagnostic rules at once is considered a bad practice. Choose specific rules/rule groups to disable instead.

rules.title: Avoid global diagnostic severity configuration
rules.desc: Configuring all diagnostic rules at once is considered a bad practice. Choose specific rules/rule groups to configure instead.

rules.title: Header must be a GLOB
rules.desc: .editorconfig files work on the premise that header texts are GLOB's matching files the key-value pairs of the section apply to. Therefore, they must be valid GLOBs.

rules.title: Use equals sign for key-value assignments
rules.desc: In .editorconfig files instead of : use = as assignment sign.

rules.title: Use global configuration for Roslyn diagnostics
rules.desc: Configuration entries intended to configure Roslyn should all be put in a the globalconfig (most likely a .globalconfig file).

rules.title: Use SLNX solution files
rules.desc: SLNX solution files are preferred over SLN files, for being less verbose and easier to read.

rules.title: Remove SLN solution files
rules.desc: SLNX solution files are preferred over SLN files, for being less verbose and easier to read. As a result, the old SLN files should be removed.

rules.title: Omit Project ID's
rules.desc: ID's are left-overs from the SLN format, and can safely be omitted.

rules.title: Included files should exist
rules.desc: Files included in a solution should exist on disk.

rules.title: Log properties visible to the compiler
rules.desc: Debug rule to show values of compiler visible properties

rules.title: Non-observed return value of the pure method.
rules.desc: Return value of pure method should be observed.

rules.title: Side effect free exception creation.
rules.desc: Newly created exceptions should be thrown or stored in variables

rules.title: Assignment-free pure object construction.
rules.desc: Newly created object was not stored form!

rules.title: Non-existing argument in the format string.
rules.desc: Argument string references an argument(s) that was not provided.

rules.title: Excessive arguments in the format string.
rules.desc: Argument was not used in the format string.

rules.title: Format argument is not a valid format string.
rules.desc: Format argument is not a valid format string.

rules.title: Regex pattern is invalid.
rules.desc: Provided regex is invalid.

rules.title: Incorrect exception propagation. Use throw; instead.
Catching everything considered harmful.
rules.desc: Generic catch block swallows an exception that was not observed.

rules.title: Only ex.Message property was observed in exception block!
Some enum cases are not covered by switch statement.
rules.desc: Switch statement that throws in default doesn't cover some cases

Explicitly enable or disable tests parallelization
rules.desc: By default, MSTest runs tests within the same assembly sequentially, which can lead to severe performance limitations. rules.title: Test classes should have valid layout
rules.desc:
Test classes, classes marked with the '[TestClass]' attribute, should respect the following layout to be considered valid by MSTest:
- it should be 'public' (or 'internal' if '[assembly: DiscoverInternals]' attribute is set)
- it should not be 'static' (except if it contains only 'AssemblyInitialize' and/or 'AssemblyCleanup' methods)
- it should not be generic.

rules.title: Test methods should have valid layout
rules.desc:
Test methods, methods marked with the '[TestMethod]' attribute, should respect the following layout to be considered valid by MSTest:
- it should be 'public' (or 'internal' if '[assembly: DiscoverInternals]' attribute is set)
- it should not be 'static'
- it should may be generic as long as type parameters can be inferred and argument types are compatible
- it should not be 'abstract'
- return type should be 'void', 'Task' or 'ValueTask'
- it should not be 'async void'
- it should not be a special method (finalizer, operator...).

rules.title: Public types should be test classes
rules.desc: It's considered a good practice to have only test classes marked public in a test project.

rules.title: Test context property should have valid layout
rules.desc:
'TestContext' should be a non-static property assigned in constructor or set by MSTest. To be set by MSTest, it should follow the layout:
- it should be 'public' regardless of whether '[assembly: DiscoverInternals]' attribute is set or not.
- it should not be 'static'
- it should have a setter.

rules.title: Avoid '[ExpectedException]'
rules.desc: Prefer 'Assert.ThrowsExactly' or 'Assert.ThrowsExactlyAsync' over '[ExpectedException]' as it ensures that only the expected call throws the expected exception. The assert APIs also provide more flexibility and allow you to assert extra properties of the exception.

Passing a value type to 'Assert.AreSame'/'Assert.AreNotSame' will be boxed (creating a new object). Because 'Assert.AreSame'/'Assert.AreNotSame' does the comparison by reference, 'Assert.AreSame' will fail when boxing happens, and 'Assert.AreNotSame' will always pass.

Do not use asserts in catch blocks
rules.desc: Using asserts in catch blocks is problematic because the test will pass even if no exception is thrown and the catch block is never executed. Use 'Assert.Throws', 'Assert.ThrowsExactly', 'Assert.ThrowsAsync' or 'Assert.ThrowsExactlyAsync' to verify that an exception is thrown, and then make additional assertions on the caught exception without using the try-catch block. The rule also flags 'throw new AssertFailedException(...)' and 'throw new AssertInconclusiveException(...)' (the desugared forms of 'Assert.Fail' and 'Assert.Inconclusive'). 'Assert.Inconclusive' (and 'throw new AssertInconclusiveException(...)') is exempt when used inside a filtered catch ('catch (...) when (...)'), because demoting a caught failure to an Inconclusive outcome is the only use case that cannot be expressed without a catch block. For other intentional bypasses (for example, attaching a runtime-built message to the failure), suppress the diagnostic with '#pragma warning disable MSTEST0058'.

rules.title: Do not use both '[Parallelize]' and '[DoNotParallelize]' attributes
rules.desc: An assembly should have either '[Parallelize]' or '[DoNotParallelize]' attribute, but not both. Having both attributes creates an ambiguous configuration. When both are present, '[DoNotParallelize]' takes precedence and parallelization will be disabled.

rules.title: Avoid duplicate test method attributes
rules.desc: A test method should be marked with exactly one attribute that is or inherits from 'TestMethodAttribute'. When multiple such attributes are present, only the first one returned by reflection will be used.

rules.title: Use '[OSCondition]' attribute instead of 'RuntimeInformation.IsOSPlatform' calls with early return or 'Assert.Inconclusive'
rules.desc: Test methods that use 'RuntimeInformation.IsOSPlatform' with early return or 'Assert.Inconclusive' should use the '[OSCondition]' attribute instead. This attribute provides a more declarative and discoverable way to specify OS-specific test requirements.

rules.title: Avoid using 'out' or 'ref' parameters in test methods
rules.desc: 'out' and 'ref' parameters add no value in test methods and they can safely be replaced by normal parameters.

rules.title: Test classes should have valid constructors
rules.desc: Test classes must have a public constructor that is either parameterless or accepts a single TestContext parameter. This allows the test framework to instantiate the test class properly.

rules.title: Prefer async assertion methods
rules.desc: When verifying exceptions from asynchronous code, use the async assertion methods instead of blocking the asynchronous operation with GetAwaiter().GetResult().

rules.title: Avoid Assert.AreEqual on collection types
rules.desc: `Assert.AreEqual` and `Assert.AreNotEqual` use `EqualityComparer<T>.Default`. For collection-like types this relies on the type's own equality semantics instead of comparing sequence elements, so `Assert.AreSequenceEqual`/`Assert.AreNotSequenceEqual` or `Assert.AreEquivalent`/`Assert.AreNotEquivalent` are usually the better fit.

rules.title: '[Ignore]' should specify a justification
rules.desc: An '[Ignore]' attribute applied to a test method or test class should include a non-empty message explaining why the test or class is ignored. A justification message makes it easier to triage skipped tests, helps reviewers understand the intent, and prevents tests from being silently disabled forever.

rules.title: Avoid synchronously blocking calls such as 'Thread.Sleep', 'Task.Wait', 'Task.WaitAll', 'Task.WaitAny' or 'Task<TResult>.Result' in test code
rules.desc: Synchronously blocking the current thread with 'Thread.Sleep', 'Task.Wait', 'Task.WaitAll', 'Task.WaitAny' or 'Task<TResult>.Result' inside test methods or test fixtures is a common source of flakiness and can also deadlock when the test framework runs tests on a SynchronizationContext that requires cooperative scheduling. Prefer 'await Task.Delay' for time-based waits and 'await' the task to observe its result.

rules.desc: The members referenced by a '[MemberCondition]' attribute must exist on the referenced type, be 'public static', return 'bool', and (for methods) be parameterless. rules.desc: Setting a 'DisplayName' on a test method to a value that is identical to the method name is redundant because the method name is already used as the display name by default. The redundant 'DisplayName' can be removed without changing how the test is reported.

rules.title: Avoid mutable static options
rules.desc: Providing a static value for MessagePackSerializerOptions from a mutable member can lead to malfunction when that member is mutated by another party.

rules.title: MessagePackObject validation

rules.title: Partial type required

Recommend adding language support to diagnostic analyzer
rules.desc: Diagnostic analyzer is marked as supporting only one language, but the analyzer assembly doesn't seem to refer to any language specific CodeAnalysis assemblies, and so is likely to work for more than one language. Consider adding an additional language argument to DiagnosticAnalyzerAttribute.

rules.title: ReportDiagnostic invoked with an unsupported DiagnosticDescriptor
rules.desc: ReportDiagnostic should only be invoked with supported DiagnosticDescriptors that are returned from DiagnosticAnalyzer.SupportedDiagnostics property. Otherwise, the reported diagnostic will be filtered out by the analysis engine.

rules.title: Invalid type argument for DiagnosticAnalyzer's Register method
rules.desc: DiagnosticAnalyzer's language-specific Register methods, such as RegisterSyntaxNodeAction, RegisterCodeBlockStartAction and RegisterCodeBlockEndAction, expect a language-specific 'SyntaxKind' type argument for it's 'TLanguageKindEnumName' type parameter. Otherwise, the registered analyzer action can never be invoked during analysis.

rules.title: Provide localizable arguments to diagnostic descriptor constructor
rules.desc: If your diagnostic analyzer and it's reported diagnostics need to be localizable, then the supported DiagnosticDescriptors used for constructing the diagnostics must also be localizable. If so, then localizable argument(s) must be provided for parameter 'title' (and optionally 'description') to the diagnostic descriptor constructor to ensure that the descriptor is localizable.

rules.title: Avoid storing per-compilation data into the fields of a diagnostic analyzer
rules.desc: Instance of a diagnostic analyzer might outlive the lifetime of compilation. Hence, storing per-compilation data, such as symbols, into the fields of a diagnostic analyzer might cause stale compilations to stay alive and cause memory leaks.  Instead, you should store this data on a separate type instantiated in a compilation start action, registered using 'AnalysisContext.RegisterCompilationStartAction' API. An instance of this type will be created per-compilation and it won't outlive compilation's lifetime, hence avoiding memory leaks.

rules.title: Only internal implementations of this interface are allowed

rules.title: Create code actions should have a unique EquivalenceKey for FixAll occurrences support
rules.desc: A CodeFixProvider that intends to support fix all occurrences must classify the registered code actions into equivalence classes by assigning it an explicit, non-null equivalence key which is unique for each kind of code action created by this fixer. This enables the FixAllProvider to fix all diagnostics in the required scope by applying code actions from this fixer that are in the equivalence class of the trigger code action.

rules.title: Use code actions that have a unique EquivalenceKey for FixAll occurrences support
rules.desc: A CodeFixProvider that intends to support fix all occurrences must classify the registered code actions into equivalence classes by assigning it an explicit, non-null equivalence key which is unique for each kind of code action created by this fixer. This enables the FixAllProvider to fix all diagnostics in the required scope by applying code actions from this fixer that are in the equivalence class of the trigger code action.

rules.title: Start action has no registered actions
rules.desc:
An analyzer start action enables performing stateful analysis over a given code unit, such as a code block, compilation, etc. Careful design is necessary to achieve efficient analyzer execution without memory leaks. Use the following guidelines for writing such analyzers:
1. Define a new scope for the registered start action, possibly with a private nested type for analyzing each code unit.
2. If required, define and initialize state in the start action.
3. Register at least one non-end action that refers to this state in the start action. If no such action is necessary, consider replacing the start action with a non-start action. For example, a CodeBlockStartAction with no registered actions or only a registered CodeBlockEndAction should be replaced with a CodeBlockAction.
4. If required, register an end action to report diagnostics based on the final state.

rules.title: Start action has no registered non-end actions
rules.desc:
An analyzer start action enables performing stateful analysis over a given code unit, such as a code block, compilation, etc. Careful design is necessary to achieve efficient analyzer execution without memory leaks. Use the following guidelines for writing such analyzers:
1. Define a new scope for the registered start action, possibly with a private nested type for analyzing each code unit.
2. If required, define and initialize state in the start action.
3. Register at least one non-end action that refers to this state in the start action. If no such action is necessary, consider replacing the start action with a non-start action. For example, a CodeBlockStartAction with no registered actions or only a registered CodeBlockEndAction should be replaced with a CodeBlockAction.
4. If required, register an end action to report diagnostics based on the final state.

rules.title: Do not invoke Compilation.GetSemanticModel() method within a diagnostic analyzer
rules.desc: 'GetSemanticModel' is an expensive method to invoke within a diagnostic analyzer because it creates a completely new semantic model, which does not share compilation data with the compiler or other analyzers. This incurs an additional performance cost during semantic analysis. Instead, consider registering a different analyzer action which allows used of a shared 'SemanticModel', such as 'RegisterOperationAction', 'RegisterSyntaxNodeAction', or 'RegisterSemanticModelAction'.

rules.desc:
The current method calls an async method that returns a Task or a Task<TResult> and doesn't apply the await operator to the result. The call to the async method starts an asynchronous task. However, because no await operator is applied, the program continues without waiting for the task to complete. In most cases, that behavior isn't what you expect. Usually other aspects of the calling method depend on the results of the call or, minimally, the called method is expected to complete before you return from the method that contains the call.

An equally important issue is what happens to exceptions that are raised in the called async method. An exception that's raised in a method that returns a Task or Task<TResult> is stored in the returned task. If you don't await the task or explicitly check for exceptions, the exception is lost. If you await the task, its exception is rethrown.

As a best practice, you should always await the call.

rules.title: Do not declare static members on generic types
rules.desc: When a static member of a generic type is called, the type argument must be specified for the type. When a generic instance member that does not support inference is called, the type argument must be specified for the member. In these two cases, the syntax for specifying the type argument is different and easily confused.

rules.title: Types that own disposable fields should be disposable
rules.desc: A class declares and implements an instance field that is a System.IDisposable type, and the class does not implement IDisposable. A class that declares an IDisposable field indirectly owns an unmanaged resource and should implement the IDisposable interface.

rules.title: Do not expose generic lists
rules.desc: System.Collections.Generic.List<T> is a generic collection that's designed for performance and not inheritance. List<T> does not contain virtual members that make it easier to change the behavior of an inherited class.

rules.title: Use generic event handler instances
rules.desc: A type contains an event that declares an EventHandler delegate that returns void, whose signature contains two parameters (the first an object and the second a type that is assignable to EventArgs), and the containing assembly targets Microsoft .NET Framework?2.0.

rules.title: Avoid excessive parameters on generic types
rules.desc: The more type parameters a generic type contains, the more difficult it is to know and remember what each type parameter represents.

rules.title: Enums should have zero value
rules.desc: The default value of an uninitialized enumeration, just as other value types, is zero. A nonflags-attributed enumeration should define a member by using the value of zero so that the default value is a valid value of the enumeration. If an enumeration that has the FlagsAttribute attribute applied defines a zero-valued member, its name should be ""None"" to indicate that no values have been set in the enumeration.

rules.title: Generic interface should also be implemented
rules.desc: To broaden the usability of a type, implement one of the generic interfaces. This is especially true for collections as they can then be used to populate generic collection types.

rules.title: Abstract types should not have public constructors
rules.desc: Constructors on abstract types can be called only by derived types. Because public constructors create instances of a type, and you cannot create instances of an abstract type, an abstract type that has a public constructor is incorrectly designed.

rules.title: Mark assemblies with CLSCompliant
rules.desc: The Common Language Specification (CLS) defines naming restrictions, data types, and rules to which assemblies must conform if they will be used across programming languages. Good design dictates that all assemblies explicitly indicate CLS compliance by using CLSCompliantAttribute . If this attribute is not present on an assembly, the assembly is not compliant.

rules.title: Mark assemblies with assembly version
rules.desc: The .NET Framework uses the version number to uniquely identify an assembly, and to bind to types in strongly named assemblies. The version number is used together with version and publisher policy. By default, applications run only with the assembly version with which they were built.

rules.title: Mark assemblies with ComVisible
rules.desc: ComVisibleAttribute determines how COM clients access managed code. Good design dictates that assemblies explicitly indicate COM visibility. COM visibility can be set for the whole assembly and then overridden for individual types and type members. If this attribute is not present, the contents of the assembly are visible to COM clients.

rules.title: Mark attributes with AttributeUsageAttribute
Define accessors for attribute arguments
Avoid out parameters
rules.desc: Passing types by reference (using 'out' or 'ref') requires experience with pointers, understanding how value types and reference types differ, and handling methods with multiple return values. Also, the difference between 'out' and 'ref' parameters is not widely understood.

rules.title: Use properties where appropriate
rules.desc: A public or protected method has a name that starts with ""Get"", takes no parameters, and returns a value that is not an array. The method might be a good candidate to become a property.

rules.title: Mark enums with FlagsAttribute
rules.desc: An enumeration is a value type that defines a set of related named constants. Apply FlagsAttribute to an enumeration when its named constants can be meaningfully combined.

rules.title: Enum Storage should be Int32
rules.desc: An enumeration is a value type that defines a set of related named constants. By default, the System.Int32 data type is used to store the constant value. Although you can change this underlying type, it is not required or recommended for most scenarios.

rules.title: Use events where appropriate
rules.desc: This rule detects methods that have names that ordinarily would be used for events. If a method is called in response to a clearly defined state change, the method should be invoked by an event handler. Objects that call the method should raise events instead of calling the method directly.

rules.title: Do not catch general exception types
rules.desc: A general exception such as System.Exception or System.SystemException or a disallowed exception type is caught in a catch statement, or a general catch clause is used. General and disallowed exceptions should not be caught.

rules.title: Implement standard exception constructors
rules.desc: Failure to provide the full set of constructors can make it difficult to correctly handle exceptions.

rules.title: Interface methods should be callable by child types
rules.desc: An unsealed externally visible type provides an explicit method implementation of a public interface and does not provide an alternative externally visible method that has the same name.

rules.title: Nested types should not be visible
rules.desc: A nested type is a type that is declared in the scope of another type. Nested types are useful to encapsulate private implementation details of the containing type. Used for this purpose, nested types should not be externally visible.

rules.title: Override methods on comparable types
rules.desc: A public or protected type implements the System.IComparable interface. It does not override Object.Equals nor does it overload the language-specific operator for equality, inequality, less than, less than or equal, greater than or greater than or equal.

rules.title: Avoid empty interfaces
rules.desc: Interfaces define members that provide a behavior or usage contract. The functionality that is described by the interface can be adopted by any type, regardless of where the type appears in the inheritance hierarchy. A type implements an interface by providing implementations for the members of the interface. An empty interface does not define any members; therefore, it does not define a contract that can be implemented.

rules.title: Provide ObsoleteAttribute message
rules.desc: A type or member is marked by using a System.ObsoleteAttribute attribute that does not have its ObsoleteAttribute.Message property specified. When a type or member that is marked by using ObsoleteAttribute is compiled, the Message property of the attribute is displayed. This gives the user information about the obsolete type or member.

rules.title: Use Integral Or String Argument For Indexers
rules.desc: Indexers, that is, indexed properties, should use integer or string types for the index. These types are typically used for indexing data structures and increase the usability of the library. Use of the Object type should be restricted to those cases where the specific integer or string type cannot be specified at design time. If the design requires other types for the index, reconsider whether the type represents a logical data store. If it does not represent a logical data store, use a method.

rules.title: Properties should not be write only
rules.desc: Although it is acceptable and often necessary to have a read-only property, the design guidelines prohibit the use of write-only properties. This is because letting a user set a value, and then preventing the user from viewing that value, does not provide any security. Also, without read access, the state of shared objects cannot be viewed, which limits their usefulness.

rules.title: Do not pass types by reference
rules.desc: Passing types by reference (using out or ref) requires experience with pointers, understanding how value types and reference types differ, and handling methods that have multiple return values. Also, the difference between out and ref parameters is not widely understood.

rules.title: Do not overload equality operator on reference types
rules.desc: For reference types, the default implementation of the equality operator is almost always correct. By default, two references are equal only if they point to the same object. If the operator is providing meaningful value equality, the type should implement the generic 'System.IEquatable' interface.

rules.title: Do not declare protected member in sealed type
rules.desc: Types declare protected members so that inheriting types can access or override the member. By definition, you cannot inherit from a sealed type, which means that protected methods on sealed types cannot be called.

rules.title: Declare types in namespaces
rules.desc: Types are declared in namespaces to prevent name collisions and as a way to organize related types in an object hierarchy.

rules.title: Do not declare visible instance fields
rules.desc: The primary use of a field should be as an implementation detail. Fields should be private or internal and should be exposed by using properties.

rules.title: Static holder types should be Static or NotInheritable
URI-like parameters should not be strings
rules.desc: This rule assumes that the parameter represents a Uniform Resource Identifier (URI). A string representation or a URI is prone to parsing and encoding errors, and can lead to security vulnerabilities. 'System.Uri' class provides these services in a safe and secure manner.

rules.title: URI-like return values should not be strings
rules.desc: This rule assumes that the method returns a URI. A string representation of a URI is prone to parsing and encoding errors, and can lead to security vulnerabilities. The System.Uri class provides these services in a safe and secure manner.

rules.title: URI-like properties should not be strings
rules.desc: This rule assumes that the property represents a Uniform Resource Identifier (URI). A string representation of a URI is prone to parsing and encoding errors, and can lead to security vulnerabilities. The System.Uri class provides these services in a safe and secure manner.

rules.title: Types should not extend certain base types
rules.desc: An externally visible type extends certain base types. Use one of the alternatives.

rules.title: Move pinvokes to native methods class
rules.desc: Platform Invocation methods, such as those that are marked by using the System.Runtime.InteropServices.DllImportAttribute attribute, or methods that are defined by using the Declare keyword in Visual Basic, access unmanaged code. These methods should be of the NativeMethods, SafeNativeMethods, or UnsafeNativeMethods class.

rules.title: Do not hide base class methods
rules.desc: A method in a base type is hidden by an identically named method in a derived type when the parameter signature of the derived method differs only by types that are more weakly derived than the corresponding types in the parameter signature of the base method.

rules.title: Validate arguments of public methods
rules.desc: An externally visible method dereferences one of its reference arguments without verifying whether that argument is 'null' ('Nothing' in Visual Basic). All reference arguments that are passed to externally visible methods should be checked against 'null'. If appropriate, throw an 'ArgumentNullException' when the argument is 'null'. If the method is designed to be called only by known assemblies, you should make the method internal.

rules.title: Implement IDisposable Correctly
rules.desc: All IDisposable types should implement the Dispose pattern correctly.

rules.title: Exceptions should be public
rules.desc: An internal exception is visible only inside its own internal scope. After the exception falls outside the internal scope, only the base exception can be used to catch the exception. If the internal exception is inherited from T:System.Exception, T:System.SystemException, or T:System.ApplicationException, the external code will not have sufficient information to know what to do with the exception.

rules.title: Do not raise exceptions in unexpected locations
rules.desc: A method that is not expected to throw exceptions throws an exception.

rules.title: Implement IEquatable when overriding Object.Equals
rules.desc: When a type T overrides Object.Equals(object), the implementation must cast the object argument to the correct type T before performing the comparison. If the type implements IEquatable<T>, and therefore offers the method T.Equals(T), and if the argument is known at compile time to be of type T, then the compiler can call IEquatable<T>.Equals(T) instead of Object.Equals(object), and no cast is necessary, improving performance.

rules.title: Override Object.Equals(object) when implementing IEquatable<T>
rules.desc: When a type T implements the interface IEquatable<T>, it suggests to a user who sees a call to the Equals method in source code that an instance of the type can be equated with an instance of any other type. The user might be confused if their attempt to equate the type with an instance of another type fails to compile. This violates the "principle of least surprise".

rules.title: CancellationToken parameters must come last
Enums values should not be duplicated
Do not declare event fields as virtual
rules.desc: Do not declare virtual events in a base class. Overridden events in a derived class have undefined behavior. The C# compiler does not handle this correctly and it is unpredictable whether a subscriber to the derived event will actually be subscribing to the base class event.

rules.title: Avoid using cref tags with a prefix
rules.desc: Use of cref tags with prefixes should be avoided, since it prevents the compiler from verifying references and the IDE from updating references during refactorings. It is permissible to suppress this error at a single documentation site if the cref must use a prefix because the type being mentioned is not findable by the compiler. For example, if a cref is mentioning a special attribute in the full framework but you're in a file that compiles against the portable framework, or if you want to reference a type at higher layer of Roslyn, you should suppress the error. You should not suppress the error just because you want to take a shortcut and avoid using the full syntax.

rules.title: Do not pass literals as localized parameters
rules.desc: A method passes a string literal as a parameter to a constructor or method in the .NET Framework class library and that string should be localizable. To fix a violation of this rule, replace the string literal with a string retrieved through an instance of the ResourceManager class.

rules.title: Specify CultureInfo
rules.desc: A method or constructor calls a member that has an overload that accepts a System.Globalization.CultureInfo parameter, and the method or constructor does not call the overload that takes the CultureInfo parameter. When a CultureInfo or System.IFormatProvider object is not supplied, the default value that is supplied by the overloaded member might not have the effect that you want in all locales. If the result will be displayed to the user, specify 'CultureInfo.CurrentCulture' as the 'CultureInfo' parameter. Otherwise, if the result will be stored and accessed by software, such as when it is persisted to disk or to a database, specify 'CultureInfo.InvariantCulture'.

rules.title: Specify IFormatProvider
rules.desc: A method or constructor calls one or more members that have overloads that accept a System.IFormatProvider parameter, and the method or constructor does not call the overload that takes the IFormatProvider parameter. When a System.Globalization.CultureInfo or IFormatProvider object is not supplied, the default value that is supplied by the overloaded member might not have the effect that you want in all locales. If the result will be based on the input from/output displayed to the user, specify 'CultureInfo.CurrentCulture' as the 'IFormatProvider'. Otherwise, if the result will be stored and accessed by software, such as when it is loaded from disk/database and when it is persisted to disk/database, specify 'CultureInfo.InvariantCulture'.

rules.title: Specify StringComparison for clarity
rules.desc: A string comparison operation uses a method overload that does not set a StringComparison parameter. It is recommended to use the overload with StringComparison parameter for clarity of intent. If the result will be displayed to the user, such as when sorting a list of items for display in a list box, specify 'StringComparison.CurrentCulture' or 'StringComparison.CurrentCultureIgnoreCase' as the 'StringComparison' parameter. If comparing case-insensitive identifiers, such as file paths, environment variables, or registry keys and values, specify 'StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase'. Otherwise, if comparing case-sensitive identifiers, specify 'StringComparison.Ordinal'.

rules.title: Normalize strings to uppercase
rules.desc: Strings should be normalized to uppercase. A small group of characters cannot make a round trip when they are converted to lowercase. To make a round trip means to convert the characters from one locale to another locale that represents character data differently, and then to accurately retrieve the original characters from the converted characters.

rules.title: Use ordinal string comparison
rules.desc: A string comparison operation that is nonlinguistic does not set the StringComparison parameter to either Ordinal or OrdinalIgnoreCase. By explicitly setting the parameter to either StringComparison.Ordinal or StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase, your code often gains speed, becomes more correct, and becomes more reliable.

rules.title: Specify StringComparison for correctness
rules.desc: A string comparison operation uses a method overload that does not set a StringComparison parameter, hence its behavior could vary based on the current user's locale settings. It is strongly recommended to use the overload with StringComparison parameter for correctness and clarity of intent. If the result will be displayed to the user, such as when sorting a list of items for display in a list box, specify 'StringComparison.CurrentCulture' or 'StringComparison.CurrentCultureIgnoreCase' as the 'StringComparison' parameter. If comparing case-insensitive identifiers, such as file paths, environment variables, or registry keys and values, specify 'StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase'. Otherwise, if comparing case-sensitive identifiers, specify 'StringComparison.Ordinal'.

rules.title: Specify a culture or use an invariant version
rules.desc: Specify culture to help avoid accidental implicit dependency on current culture. Using an invariant version yields consistent results regardless of the culture of an application.

rules.title: P/Invokes should not be visible
rules.desc: A public or protected method in a public type has the System.Runtime.InteropServices.DllImportAttribute attribute (also implemented by the Declare keyword in Visual Basic). Such methods should not be exposed.

rules.title: Validate platform compatibility
rules.desc: Using platform dependent API on a component makes the code no longer work across all platforms.

rules.title: Do not use 'OutAttribute' on string parameters for P/Invokes
rules.desc: String parameters passed by value with the 'OutAttribute' can destabilize the runtime if the string is an interned string.

rules.title: Use valid platform string
rules.desc: Platform compatibility analyzer requires a valid platform name and version.

rules.title: Provide a parameterless constructor that is as visible as the containing type for concrete types derived from 'System.Runtime.InteropServices.SafeHandle'
rules.desc: Providing a parameterless constructor that is as visible as the containing type for a type derived from 'System.Runtime.InteropServices.SafeHandle' enables better performance and usage with source-generated interop solutions.

rules.title: Property, type, or attribute requires runtime marshalling
rules.desc: Using features that require runtime marshalling when runtime marshalling is disabled will result in runtime exceptions.

rules.title: This method uses runtime marshalling even when the 'DisableRuntimeMarshallingAttribute' is applied
rules.desc: This method uses runtime marshalling even when runtime marshalling is disabled, which can cause unexpected behavior differences at runtime due to different expectations of a type's native layout.

rules.title: Validate platform compatibility
rules.desc: Using platform dependent API on a component makes the code no longer work across all platforms.

rules.title: Avoid excessive inheritance
rules.desc: Deeply nested type hierarchies can be difficult to follow, understand, and maintain. This rule limits analysis to hierarchies in the same module. To fix a violation of this rule, derive the type from a base type that is less deep in the inheritance hierarchy or eliminate some of the intermediate base types.

rules.title: Avoid excessive complexity
rules.desc: Cyclomatic complexity measures the number of linearly independent paths through the method, which is determined by the number and complexity of conditional branches. A low cyclomatic complexity generally indicates a method that is easy to understand, test, and maintain. The cyclomatic complexity is calculated from a control flow graph of the method and is given as follows: `cyclomatic complexity = the number of edges - the number of nodes + 1`, where a node represents a logic branch point and an edge represents a line between nodes.

rules.title: Avoid unmaintainable code
rules.desc: The maintainability index is calculated by using the following metrics: lines of code, program volume, and cyclomatic complexity. Program volume is a measure of the difficulty of understanding of a symbol that is based on the number of operators and operands in the code. Cyclomatic complexity is a measure of the structural complexity of the type or method. A low maintainability index indicates that code is probably difficult to maintain and would be a good candidate to redesign.

rules.title: Avoid excessive class coupling
rules.desc: This rule measures class coupling by counting the number of unique type references that a symbol contains. Symbols that have a high degree of class coupling can be difficult to maintain. It is a good practice to have types and methods that exhibit low coupling and high cohesion. To fix this violation, try to redesign the code to reduce the number of types to which it is coupled.

rules.title: Use nameof to express symbol names
rules.desc: Using nameof helps keep your code valid when refactoring.

rules.title: Avoid dead conditional code
Invalid entry in code metrics rule specification file
rules.desc: Invalid entry in code metrics rule specification file.

rules.title: Use ArgumentNullException throw helper
rules.desc: Throw helpers are simpler and more efficient than an if block constructing a new exception instance.

rules.title: Use ArgumentException throw helper
rules.desc: Throw helpers are simpler and more efficient than an if block constructing a new exception instance.

rules.title: Use ArgumentOutOfRangeException throw helper
rules.desc: Throw helpers are simpler and more efficient than an if block constructing a new exception instance.

rules.title: Use ObjectDisposedException throw helper
rules.desc: Throw helpers are simpler and more efficient than an if block constructing a new exception instance.

rules.title: Avoid redundant length argument
rules.desc: An explicit length calculation can be error-prone and can be avoided when slicing to end of the buffer.

rules.title: Consider making public types internal
rules.desc: Unlike a class library, an application's API isn't typically referenced publicly, so types can be marked internal.

rules.title: Use cross-platform intrinsics
rules.desc: This rule detects usage of platform-specific intrinsics that can be replaced with an equivalent cross-platform intrinsic instead.

rules.title: Do not name enum values 'Reserved'
rules.desc: This rule assumes that an enumeration member that has a name that contains "reserved" is not currently used but is a placeholder to be renamed or removed in a future version. Renaming or removing a member is a breaking change.

rules.title: Identifiers should not contain underscores
rules.desc: By convention, identifier names do not contain the underscore (_) character. This rule checks namespaces, types, members, and parameters.

rules.title: Identifiers should differ by more than case
rules.desc: Identifiers for namespaces, types, members, and parameters cannot differ only by case because languages that target the common language runtime are not required to be case-sensitive.

rules.title: Identifiers should have correct suffix
rules.desc: By convention, the names of types that extend certain base types or that implement certain interfaces, or types that are derived from these types, have a suffix that is associated with the base type or interface.

rules.title: Identifiers should not have incorrect suffix
rules.desc: By convention, only the names of types that extend certain base types or that implement certain interfaces, or types that are derived from these types, should end with specific reserved suffixes. Other type names should not use these reserved suffixes.

rules.title: Do not prefix enum values with type name
rules.desc: An enumeration's values should not start with the type name of the enumeration.

rules.title: Events should not have 'Before' or 'After' prefix
rules.desc: Event names should describe the action that raises the event. To name related events that are raised in a specific sequence, use the present or past tense to indicate the relative position in the sequence of actions. For example, when naming a pair of events that is raised when closing a resource, you might name it 'Closing' and 'Closed', instead of 'BeforeClose' and 'AfterClose'.

rules.title: Identifiers should have correct prefix
rules.desc: The name of an externally visible interface does not start with an uppercase ""I"". The name of a generic type parameter on an externally visible type or method does not start with an uppercase ""T"".

rules.title: Identifiers should not match keywords
rules.desc: A namespace name or a type name matches a reserved keyword in a programming language. Identifiers for namespaces and types should not match keywords that are defined by languages that target the common language runtime.

rules.title: Identifier contains type name
rules.desc: Names of parameters and members are better used to communicate their meaning than to describe their type, which is expected to be provided by development tools. For names of members, if a data type name must be used, use a language-independent name instead of a language-specific one.

rules.title: Property names should not match get methods
rules.desc: The name of a public or protected member starts with ""Get"" and otherwise matches the name of a public or protected property. ""Get"" methods and properties should have names that clearly distinguish their function.

rules.title: Type names should not match namespaces
rules.desc: Type names should not match the names of namespaces that are defined in the .NET Framework class library. Violating this rule can reduce the usability of the library.

rules.title: Parameter names should match base declaration
rules.desc: Consistent naming of parameters in an override hierarchy increases the usability of the method overrides. A parameter name in a derived method that differs from the name in the base declaration can cause confusion about whether the method is an override of the base method or a new overload of the method.

rules.title: Use PascalCase for named placeholders
rules.desc: Use PascalCase for named placeholders in the logging message template.

rules.title: Review unused parameters
rules.desc: Avoid unused paramereters in your code. If the parameter cannot be removed, then change its name so it starts with an underscore and is optionally followed by an integer, such as '_', '_1', '_2', etc. These are treated as special discard symbol names.

rules.title: Use literals where appropriate
rules.desc: A field is declared static and read-only (Shared and ReadOnly in Visual Basic), and is initialized by using a value that is computable at compile time. Because the value that is assigned to the targeted field is computable at compile time, change the declaration to a const (Const in Visual Basic) field so that the value is computed at compile time instead of at runtime.

rules.title: Do not initialize unnecessarily
rules.desc: The .NET runtime initializes all fields of reference types to their default values before running the constructor. In most cases, explicitly initializing a field to its default value in a constructor is redundant, adding maintenance costs and potentially degrading performance (such as with increased assembly size), and the explicit initialization can be removed.  In some cases, such as with static readonly fields that permanently retain their default value, consider instead changing them to be constants or properties.

rules.title: Do not ignore method results
rules.desc: A new object is created but never used; or a method that creates and returns a new string is called and the new string is never used; or a COM or P/Invoke method returns an HRESULT or error code that is never used.

rules.title: Initialize reference type static fields inline
rules.desc: A reference type declares an explicit static constructor. To fix a violation of this rule, initialize all static data when it is declared and remove the static constructor.

rules.title: Avoid uninstantiated internal classes
rules.desc: An instance of an assembly-level type is not created by code in the assembly.

rules.title: Avoid unsealed attributes
rules.desc: The .NET Framework class library provides methods for retrieving custom attributes. By default, these methods search the attribute inheritance hierarchy. Sealing the attribute eliminates the search through the inheritance hierarchy and can improve performance.

rules.title: Prefer jagged arrays over multidimensional
rules.desc: A jagged array is an array whose elements are arrays. The arrays that make up the elements can be of different sizes, leading to less wasted space for some sets of data.

rules.title: Override equals and operator equals on value types
rules.desc: For value types, the inherited implementation of Equals uses the Reflection library and compares the contents of all fields. Reflection is computationally expensive, and comparing every field for equality might be unnecessary. If you expect users to compare or sort instances, or to use instances as hash table keys, your value type should implement Equals.

rules.title: Dispose methods should call SuppressFinalize
rules.desc: A method that is an implementation of Dispose does not call GC.SuppressFinalize; or a method that is not an implementation of Dispose calls GC.SuppressFinalize; or a method calls GC.SuppressFinalize and passes something other than this (Me in Visual Basic).

rules.title: Properties should not return arrays
rules.desc: Arrays that are returned by properties are not write-protected, even when the property is read-only. To keep the array tamper-proof, the property must return a copy of the array. Typically, users will not understand the adverse performance implications of calling such a property.

rules.title: Test for empty strings using string length
rules.desc: Comparing strings by using the String.Length property or the String.IsNullOrEmpty method is significantly faster than using Equals.

rules.title: Remove empty Finalizers
rules.desc: Finalizers should be avoided where possible, to avoid the additional performance overhead involved in tracking object lifetime.

rules.title: Mark members as static
rules.desc: Members that do not access instance data or call instance methods can be marked as static. After you mark the methods as static, the compiler will emit nonvirtual call sites to these members. This can give you a measurable performance gain for performance-sensitive code.

rules.title: Avoid unused private fields
rules.desc: Private fields were detected that do not appear to be accessed in the assembly.

rules.title: Mark assemblies with NeutralResourcesLanguageAttribute
rules.desc: The NeutralResourcesLanguage attribute informs the ResourceManager of the language that was used to display the resources of a neutral culture for an assembly. This improves lookup performance for the first resource that you load and can reduce your working set.

rules.title: Avoid zero-length array allocations
Do not use Enumerable methods on indexable collections
rules.desc: This collection is directly indexable. Going through LINQ here causes unnecessary allocations and CPU work.

rules.title: Do not use Count() or LongCount() when Any() can be used
rules.desc: For non-empty collections, Count() and LongCount() enumerate the entire sequence, while Any() stops at the first item or the first item that satisfies a condition.

rules.title: Do not use CountAsync() or LongCountAsync() when AnyAsync() can be used
rules.desc: For non-empty collections, CountAsync() and LongCountAsync() enumerate the entire sequence, while AnyAsync() stops at the first item or the first item that satisfies a condition.

rules.title: Use Length/Count property instead of Count() when available
rules.desc: Enumerable.Count() potentially enumerates the sequence while a Length/Count property is a direct access.

rules.title: Prefer strongly-typed Append and Insert method overloads on StringBuilder
rules.desc: StringBuilder.Append and StringBuilder.Insert provide overloads for multiple types beyond System.String.  When possible, prefer the strongly-typed overloads over using ToString() and the string-based overload.

rules.title: Use AsSpan or AsMemory instead of Range-based indexers when appropriate
rules.desc: The Range-based indexer on string values produces a copy of requested portion of the string. This copy is usually unnecessary when it is implicitly used as a ReadOnlySpan or ReadOnlyMemory value. Use the AsSpan method to avoid the unnecessary copy.

rules.title: Use AsSpan or AsMemory instead of Range-based indexers when appropriate
rules.desc: The Range-based indexer on array values produces a copy of requested portion of the array. This copy is usually unnecessary when it is implicitly used as a ReadOnlySpan or ReadOnlyMemory value. Use the AsSpan method to avoid the unnecessary copy.

rules.title: Use AsSpan or AsMemory instead of Range-based indexers when appropriate
rules.desc: The Range-based indexer on array values produces a copy of requested portion of the array. This copy is often unwanted when it is implicitly used as a Span or Memory value. Use the AsSpan method to avoid the copy.

rules.title: Consider using 'StringBuilder.Append(char)' when applicable
rules.desc: 'StringBuilder.Append(char)' is more efficient than 'StringBuilder.Append(string)' when the string is a single character. When calling 'Append' with a constant, prefer using a constant char rather than a constant string containing one character.

rules.title: Prefer the 'Memory'-based overloads for 'ReadAsync' and 'WriteAsync'
rules.desc: 'Stream' has a 'ReadAsync' overload that takes a 'Memory<Byte>' as the first argument, and a 'WriteAsync' overload that takes a 'ReadOnlyMemory<Byte>' as the first argument. Prefer calling the memory based overloads, which are more efficient.

rules.title: Prefer IsEmpty over Count
rules.desc: For determining whether the object contains or not any items, prefer using 'IsEmpty' property rather than retrieving the number of items from the 'Count' property and comparing it to 0 or 1.

rules.title: Use 'Environment.ProcessId'
rules.desc: 'Environment.ProcessId' is simpler and faster than 'Process.GetCurrentProcess().Id'.

rules.title: Avoid 'StringBuilder' parameters for P/Invokes
rules.desc: Marshalling of 'StringBuilder' always creates a native buffer copy, resulting in multiple allocations for one marshalling operation.

rules.title: Use 'Environment.ProcessPath'
rules.desc: 'Environment.ProcessPath' is simpler and faster than 'Process.GetCurrentProcess().MainModule.FileName'.

rules.title: Use 'Environment.CurrentManagedThreadId'
rules.desc: 'Environment.CurrentManagedThreadId' is simpler and faster than 'Thread.CurrentThread.ManagedThreadId'.

rules.title: Prefer Dictionary.Contains methods
rules.desc: Many dictionary implementations lazily initialize the Values collection. To avoid unnecessary allocations, prefer 'ContainsValue' over 'Values.Contains'.

rules.title: Do not use 'WhenAll' with a single task
rules.desc: Using 'WhenAll' with a single task may result in performance loss, await or return the task instead.

rules.title: Do not use 'WaitAll' with a single task
rules.desc: Using 'WaitAll' with a single task may result in performance loss, await or return the task instead.

rules.title: Provide memory-based overrides of async methods when subclassing 'Stream'
rules.desc: To improve performance, override the memory-based async methods when subclassing 'Stream'. Then implement the array-based methods in terms of the memory-based methods.

rules.title: Use span-based 'string.Concat'
rules.desc: It is more efficient to use 'AsSpan' and 'string.Concat', instead of 'Substring' and a concatenation operator.

rules.title: Prefer 'AsSpan' over 'Substring'
rules.desc: 'AsSpan' is more efficient than 'Substring'. 'Substring' performs an O(n) string copy, while 'AsSpan' does not and has a constant cost.

rules.title: Use char literal for a single character lookup
rules.desc: 'string.Contains(char)' is available as a better performing overload for single char lookup.

rules.title: Use the LoggerMessage delegates
rules.desc: For improved performance, use the LoggerMessage delegates.

rules.title: Call async methods when in an async method
rules.desc: When inside a Task-returning method, use the async version of methods, if they exist.

rules.title: Prefer static 'HashData' method over 'ComputeHash'
rules.desc: It is more efficient to use the static 'HashData' method over creating and managing a HashAlgorithm instance to call 'ComputeHash'.

rules.title: Possible multiple enumerations of 'IEnumerable' collection
Seal internal types
rules.desc: When a type is not accessible outside its assembly and has no subtypes within its containing assembly, it can be safely sealed. Sealing types can improve performance.

rules.title: Unnecessary call to 'Dictionary.ContainsKey(key)'
rules.desc: Do not guard 'Dictionary.Remove(key)' with 'Dictionary.ContainsKey(key)'. The former already checks whether the key exists, and will not throw if it does not.

rules.title: Prefer the 'IDictionary.TryGetValue(TKey, out TValue)' method
rules.desc: Prefer a 'TryGetValue' call over a Dictionary indexer access guarded by a 'ContainsKey' check. 'ContainsKey' and the indexer both would lookup the key under the hood, so using 'TryGetValue' removes the extra lookup.

rules.title: Prefer 'Clear' over 'Fill'
rules.desc: It is more efficient to use 'Clear', instead of 'Fill' with default value.

rules.title: Incorrect usage of ConstantExpected attribute
rules.desc: ConstantExpected attribute is not applied correctly on the parameter.

rules.title: A constant is expected for the parameter
rules.desc: The parameter expects a constant for optimal performance.

rules.title: Use 'StartsWith' instead of 'IndexOf'
rules.desc: It is both clearer and faster to use 'StartsWith' instead of comparing the result of 'IndexOf' to zero.

rules.title: Use concrete types when possible for improved performance
rules.desc: Using concrete types avoids virtual or interface call overhead and enables inlining.

rules.title: Avoid using 'Enumerable.Any()' extension method
rules.desc: Prefer using 'IsEmpty', 'Count' or 'Length' properties whichever available, rather than calling 'Enumerable.Any()'. The intent is clearer and it is more performant than using 'Enumerable.Any()' extension method.

rules.title: Avoid constant arrays as arguments
rules.desc: Constant arrays passed as arguments are not reused when called repeatedly, which implies a new array is created each time. Consider extracting them to 'static readonly' fields to improve performance if the passed array is not mutated within the called method.

rules.title: Use the 'StringComparison' method overloads to perform case-insensitive string comparisons
rules.desc: Avoid calling 'ToLower', 'ToUpper', 'ToLowerInvariant' and 'ToUpperInvariant' to perform case-insensitive string comparisons, as in 'string.ToLower() == string.ToLower()', because they lead to an allocation. Instead, use 'string.Equals(string, StringComparison)' to perform case-insensitive comparisons. Switching to using an overload that takes a 'StringComparison' might cause subtle changes in behavior, so it's important to conduct thorough testing after applying the suggestion. Additionally, if a culturally sensitive comparison is not required, consider using 'StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase'.

rules.title: Use 'CompositeFormat'
rules.desc: Cache and use a 'CompositeFormat' instance as the argument to this formatting operation, rather than passing in the original format string. This reduces the cost of the formatting operation.

rules.title: Prefer the 'IDictionary.TryAdd(TKey, TValue)' method
