rules.desc: Prefer a 'TryAdd' call over an 'Add' call guarded by a 'ContainsKey' check. 'TryAdd' behaves the same as 'Add', except that when the specified key already exists, it returns 'false' instead of throwing an exception.

rules.title: Use char overload
rules.desc: The char overload is a better performing overload than a string with a single char.

rules.title: Use char overload
rules.desc: The char overload is a better performing overload than a string with a single char.

rules.title: Use char overload
rules.desc: The char overload is a better performing overload than a string with a single char.

rules.title: Unnecessary call to 'Contains(item)'
rules.desc: Do not guard 'Add(item)' or 'Remove(item)' with 'Contains(item)' for the set. The former two already check whether the item exists and will return if it was added or removed.

rules.title: Cache and reuse 'JsonSerializerOptions' instances
rules.desc: Avoid creating a new 'JsonSerializerOptions' instance for every serialization operation. Cache and reuse instances instead. Single use 'JsonSerializerOptions' instances can substantially degrade the performance of your application.

rules.title: Use a cached 'SearchValues' instance
rules.desc: Using a cached 'SearchValues' instance is more efficient than passing values to 'IndexOfAny'/'ContainsAny' directly.

rules.title: Do not pass a nullable struct to 'ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull'
rules.desc: 'ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull' accepts an 'object', so passing a nullable struct may cause the value to be boxed.

rules.title: Prefer 'Convert.ToHexString' and 'Convert.ToHexStringLower' over call chains based on 'BitConverter.ToString'
rules.desc: Use 'Convert.ToHexString' or 'Convert.ToHexStringLower' when encoding bytes to a hexadecimal string representation. These methods are more efficient and allocation-friendly than using 'BitConverter.ToString' in combination with 'String.Replace' to replace dashes and 'String.ToLower'.

rules.title: Avoid potentially expensive logging
rules.desc: In many situations, logging is disabled or set to a log level that results in an unnecessary evaluation for this argument.

rules.title: Use 'Regex.IsMatch'
rules.desc: 'Regex.IsMatch' is simpler and faster than 'Regex.Match(...).Success'.

rules.title: Use 'Regex.Count'
rules.desc: 'Regex.Count' is simpler and faster than 'Regex.Matches(...).Count'.

rules.title: Dispose objects before losing scope
rules.desc: If a disposable object is not explicitly disposed before all references to it are out of scope, the object will be disposed at some indeterminate time when the garbage collector runs the finalizer of the object. Because an exceptional event might occur that will prevent the finalizer of the object from running, the object should be explicitly disposed instead.

rules.title: Do not lock on objects with weak identity
rules.desc: An object is said to have a weak identity when it can be directly accessed across application domain boundaries. A thread that tries to acquire a lock on an object that has a weak identity can be blocked by a second thread in a different application domain that has a lock on the same object.

rules.title: Consider calling ConfigureAwait on the awaited task
rules.desc: When an asynchronous method awaits a Task directly, continuation occurs in the same thread that created the task. Consider calling Task.ConfigureAwait(Boolean) to signal your intention for continuation. Call ConfigureAwait(false) on the task to schedule continuations to the thread pool, thereby avoiding a deadlock on the UI thread. Passing false is a good option for app-independent libraries. Calling ConfigureAwait(true) on the task has the same behavior as not explicitly calling ConfigureAwait. By explicitly calling this method, you're letting readers know you intentionally want to perform the continuation on the original synchronization context.

rules.title: Do not create tasks without passing a TaskScheduler
rules.desc: Do not create tasks unless you are using one of the overloads that takes a TaskScheduler. The default is to schedule on TaskScheduler.Current, which would lead to deadlocks. Either use TaskScheduler.Default to schedule on the thread pool, or explicitly pass TaskScheduler.Current to make your intentions clear.

rules.title: Do not call ToImmutableCollection on an ImmutableCollection value
Avoid infinite recursion
Use ValueTasks correctly
rules.desc: ValueTasks returned from member invocations are intended to be directly awaited.  Attempts to consume a ValueTask multiple times or to directly access one's result before it's known to be completed may result in an exception or corruption.  Ignoring such a ValueTask is likely an indication of a functional bug and may degrade performance.

rules.title: Do not use ReferenceEquals with value types
rules.desc: Value type typed arguments are uniquely boxed for each call to this method, therefore the result can be unexpected.

rules.title: Do not use stackalloc in loops
rules.desc: Stack space allocated by a stackalloc is only released at the end of the current method's invocation.  Using it in a loop can result in unbounded stack growth and eventual stack overflow conditions.

rules.title: Do not define finalizers for types derived from MemoryManager<T>
rules.desc: Adding a finalizer to a type derived from MemoryManager<T> may permit memory to be freed while it is still in use by a Span<T>.

rules.title: Forward the 'CancellationToken' parameter to methods
rules.desc: Forward the 'CancellationToken' parameter to methods to ensure the operation cancellation notifications gets properly propagated, or pass in 'CancellationToken.None' explicitly to indicate intentionally not propagating the token.

rules.title: Parameter count mismatch
rules.desc: Number of parameters supplied in the logging message template do not match the number of named placeholders.

rules.title: 'Buffer.BlockCopy' expects the number of bytes to be copied for the 'count' argument
rules.desc: 'Buffer.BlockCopy' expects the number of bytes to be copied for the 'count' argument. Using 'Array.Length' may not match the number of bytes that needs to be copied.

rules.title: Improper 'ThreadStatic' field initialization
rules.desc: 'ThreadStatic' fields should be initialized lazily on use, not with inline initialization nor explicitly in a static constructor, which would only initialize the field on the thread that runs the type's static constructor.

rules.title: Prevent behavioral change
rules.desc: Some built-in operators added in .NET 7 behave differently when overflowing than did the corresponding user-defined operators in .NET 6 and earlier versions. Some operators that previously threw in an unchecked context now don't throw unless wrapped within a checked context. Also, some operators that did not previously throw in a checked context now throw unless wrapped in an unchecked context.

rules.title: Do not call Enumerable.Cast<T> or Enumerable.OfType<T> with incompatible types
rules.desc:
Enumerable.Cast<T> and Enumerable.OfType<T> require compatible types to function expectedly.  
The generic cast (IL 'unbox.any') used by the sequence returned by Enumerable.Cast<T> will throw InvalidCastException at runtime on elements of the types specified.  
The generic type check (C# 'is' operator/IL 'isinst') used by Enumerable.OfType<T> will never succeed with elements of types specified, resulting in an empty sequence.  
Widening and user defined conversions are not supported with generic types.

rules.title: Avoid inexact read with 'Stream.Read'
rules.desc: A call to 'Stream.Read' may return fewer bytes than requested, resulting in unreliable code if the return value is not checked.

rules.title: Invalid braces in message template
rules.desc: The braces present in the message template are invalid. Ensure any braces in the message template are valid opening/closing braces, or are escaped.

rules.title: Do not use 'StreamReader.EndOfStream' in async methods
rules.desc: The property 'StreamReader.EndOfStream' can cause unintended synchronous blocking when no data is buffered. Instead, use 'StreamReader.ReadLineAsync' directly, which returns 'null' when reaching the end of the stream.

rules.title: Do not pass 'IDisposable' instances into unawaited tasks
rules.desc: Unawaited tasks that use 'IDisposable' instances may use those instances long after they have been disposed. Ensure tasks using those instances are completed before the instances are disposed.

rules.title: Review SQL queries for security vulnerabilities
rules.desc: SQL queries that directly use user input can be vulnerable to SQL injection attacks. Review this SQL query for potential vulnerabilities, and consider using a parameterized SQL query.

rules.title: Specify marshaling for P/Invoke string arguments
rules.desc: A platform invoke member allows partially trusted callers, has a string parameter, and does not explicitly marshal the string. This can cause a potential security vulnerability.

rules.title: Review visible event handlers
rules.desc: A public or protected event-handling method was detected. Event-handling methods should not be exposed unless absolutely necessary.

rules.title: Seal methods that satisfy private interfaces
rules.desc: An inheritable public type provides an overridable method implementation of an internal (Friend in Visual Basic) interface. To fix a violation of this rule, prevent the method from being overridden outside the assembly.

rules.title: Do Not Catch Corrupted State Exceptions
rules.desc: Catching corrupted state exceptions could mask errors (such as access violations), resulting in inconsistent state of execution or making it easier for attackers to compromise system. Instead, catch and handle a more specific set of exception type(s) or re-throw the exception.

rules.title: Rethrow to preserve stack details
Do not raise reserved exception types
rules.desc: An exception of type that is not sufficiently specific or reserved by the runtime should never be raised by user code. This makes the original error difficult to detect and debug. If this exception instance might be thrown, use a different exception type.

rules.title: Initialize value type static fields inline
rules.desc: A value type declares an explicit static constructor. To fix a violation of this rule, initialize all static data when it is declared and remove the static constructor.

rules.title: Instantiate argument exceptions correctly
rules.desc: A call is made to the default (parameterless) constructor of an exception type that is or derives from ArgumentException, or an incorrect string argument is passed to a parameterized constructor of an exception type that is or derives from ArgumentException.

rules.title: Non-constant fields should not be visible
rules.desc: Static fields that are neither constants nor read-only are not thread-safe. Access to such a field must be carefully controlled and requires advanced programming techniques to synchronize access to the class object.

rules.title: Disposable fields should be disposed
rules.desc: A type that implements System.IDisposable declares fields that are of types that also implement IDisposable. The Dispose method of the field is not called by the Dispose method of the declaring type. To fix a violation of this rule, call Dispose on fields that are of types that implement IDisposable if you are responsible for allocating and releasing the unmanaged resources held by the field.

rules.title: Do not call overridable methods in constructors
rules.desc: Virtual methods defined on the class should not be called from constructors. If a derived class has overridden the method, the derived class version will be called (before the derived class constructor is called).

rules.title: Dispose methods should call base class dispose
rules.desc: A type that implements System.IDisposable inherits from a type that also implements IDisposable. The Dispose method of the inheriting type does not call the Dispose method of the parent type. To fix a violation of this rule, call base.Dispose in your Dispose method.

rules.title: Disposable types should declare finalizer
rules.desc: A type that implements System.IDisposable and has fields that suggest the use of unmanaged resources does not implement a finalizer, as described by Object.Finalize.

rules.title: Do not mark enums with FlagsAttribute
rules.desc: An externally visible enumeration is marked by using FlagsAttribute, and it has one or more values that are not powers of two or a combination of the other defined values on the enumeration.

rules.title: Override GetHashCode on overriding Equals
rules.desc: GetHashCode returns a value, based on the current instance, that is suited for hashing algorithms and data structures such as a hash table. Two objects that are the same type and are equal must return the same hash code.

rules.title: Do not raise exceptions in finally clauses
rules.desc: When an exception is raised in a finally clause, the new exception hides the active exception. This makes the original error difficult to detect and debug.

rules.title: Override Equals on overloading operator equals
rules.desc: A public type implements the equality operator but does not override Object.Equals.

rules.title: Operator overloads have named alternates
rules.desc: An operator overload was detected, and the expected named alternative method was not found. The named alternative member provides access to the same functionality as the operator and is provided for developers who program in languages that do not support overloaded operators.

rules.title: Operators should have symmetrical overloads
rules.desc: A type implements the equality or inequality operator and does not implement the opposite operator.

rules.title: Collection properties should be read only
rules.desc: A writable collection property allows a user to replace the collection with a different collection. A read-only property stops the collection from being replaced but still allows the individual members to be set.

rules.title: Implement serialization constructors
rules.desc: To fix a violation of this rule, implement the serialization constructor. For a sealed class, make the constructor private; otherwise, make it protected.

rules.title: Overload operator equals on overriding value type Equals
rules.desc: In most programming languages there is no default implementation of the equality operator (==) for value types. If your programming language supports operator overloads, you should consider implementing the equality operator. Its behavior should be identical to that of Equals.

rules.title: Pass system uri objects instead of strings
rules.desc: A call is made to a method that has a string parameter whose name contains "uri", "URI", "urn", "URN", "url", or "URL". The declaring type of the method contains a corresponding method overload that has a System.Uri parameter.

rules.title: Mark all non-serializable fields
rules.desc: An instance field of a type that is not serializable is declared in a type that is serializable.

rules.title: Mark ISerializable types with serializable
rules.desc: To be recognized by the common language runtime as serializable, types must be marked by using the SerializableAttribute attribute even when the type uses a custom serialization routine through implementation of the ISerializable interface.

rules.title: Provide correct arguments to formatting methods
rules.desc: The format argument that is passed to System.String.Format does not contain a format item that corresponds to each object argument, or vice versa.

rules.title: Test for NaN correctly
rules.desc: This expression tests a value against Single.Nan or Double.Nan. Use Single.IsNan(Single) or Double.IsNan(Double) to test the value.

rules.title: Attribute string literals should parse correctly
rules.desc: The string literal parameter of an attribute does not parse correctly for a URL, a GUID, or a version.

rules.title: Do not duplicate indexed element initializations
rules.desc: Indexed elements in objects initializers must initialize unique elements. A duplicate index might overwrite a previous element initialization.

rules.title: Do not assign a property to itself
Assigning symbol and its member in the same statement
rules.desc: Assigning to a symbol and its member (field/property) in the same statement is not recommended. It is not clear if the member access was intended to use symbol's old value prior to the assignment or new value from the assignment in this statement. For clarity, consider splitting the assignments into separate statements.

rules.title: Argument passed to TaskCompletionSource constructor should be TaskCreationOptions enum instead of TaskContinuationOptions enum
rules.desc: TaskCompletionSource has constructors that take TaskCreationOptions that control the underlying Task, and constructors that take object state that's stored in the task.  Accidentally passing a TaskContinuationOptions instead of a TaskCreationOptions will result in the call treating the options as state.

rules.title: Provide correct 'enum' argument to 'Enum.HasFlag'
rules.desc: 'Enum.HasFlag' method expects the 'enum' argument to be of the same 'enum' type as the instance on which the method is invoked and that this 'enum' is marked with 'System.FlagsAttribute'. If these are different 'enum' types, an unhandled exception will be thrown at runtime. If the 'enum' type is not marked with 'System.FlagsAttribute' the call will always return 'false' at runtime.

rules.title: Consider using 'string.Contains' instead of 'string.IndexOf'
rules.desc: Calls to 'string.IndexOf' where the result is used to check for the presence/absence of a substring can be replaced by 'string.Contains'.

rules.title: Use 'ThrowIfCancellationRequested'
rules.desc: 'ThrowIfCancellationRequested' automatically checks whether the token has been canceled, and throws an 'OperationCanceledException' if it has.

rules.title: Use 'string.Equals'
rules.desc: It is both clearer and likely faster to use 'string.Equals' instead of comparing the result of 'string.Compare' to zero.

rules.title: This API requires opting into preview features
rules.desc: An assembly has to opt into preview features before using them.

rules.title: Named placeholders should not be numeric values
rules.desc: Named placeholders in the logging message template should not be comprised of only numeric characters.

rules.title: Template should be a static expression
rules.desc: The logging message template should not vary between calls.

rules.title: The 'ModuleInitializer' attribute should not be used in libraries
rules.desc: Module initializers are intended to be used by application code to ensure an application's components are initialized before the application code begins executing. If library code declares a method with the 'ModuleInitializerAttribute', it can interfere with application initialization and also lead to limitations in that application's trimming abilities. Instead of using methods marked with 'ModuleInitializerAttribute', the library should expose methods that can be used to initialize any components within the library and allow the application to invoke the method during application initialization.

rules.title: All members declared in parent interfaces must have an implementation in a DynamicInterfaceCastableImplementation-attributed interface
rules.desc: Types attributed with 'DynamicInterfaceCastableImplementationAttribute' act as an interface implementation for a type that implements the 'IDynamicInterfaceCastable' type. As a result, it must provide an implementation of all of the members defined in the inherited interfaces, because the type that implements 'IDynamicInterfaceCastable' will not provide them otherwise.

rules.title: Members defined on an interface with the 'DynamicInterfaceCastableImplementationAttribute' should be 'static'
rules.desc: Since a type that implements 'IDynamicInterfaceCastable' may not implement a dynamic interface in metadata, calls to an instance interface member that is not an explicit implementation defined on this type are likely to fail at runtime. Mark new interface members 'static' to avoid runtime errors.

rules.title: Providing a 'DynamicInterfaceCastableImplementation' interface in Visual Basic is unsupported
rules.desc: Providing a functional 'DynamicInterfaceCastableImplementationAttribute'-attributed interface requires the Default Interface Members feature, which is unsupported in Visual Basic.

rules.title: 'ThreadStatic' only affects static fields
rules.desc: 'ThreadStatic' only affects static fields. When applied to instance fields, it has no impact on behavior.

rules.title: Use correct type parameter
rules.desc: Generic math interfaces require the derived type itself to be used for the self recurring type parameter.

rules.title: Do not use ConfigureAwaitOptions.SuppressThrowing with Task<TResult>
rules.desc: The ConfigureAwaitOptions.SuppressThrowing option is only supported with the non-generic Task, not a Task<TResult>.  To use it with a Task<TResult>, first cast to the base Task.

rules.title: Set 'MaxResponseHeadersLength' properly
rules.desc: The property 'MaxResponseHeadersLength' is measured in kilobytes, not in bytes. The provided value is multiplied by 1024, which might be greater than your intended maximum length.

rules.title: Prefer generic overload when type is known
rules.desc: Using a generic overload is preferable to the 'System.Type' overload when the type is known, promoting cleaner and more type-safe code with improved compile-time checks.

rules.title: Do not pass a non-nullable value to 'ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull'
rules.desc: 'ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull' throws when the passed argument is 'null'. Certain constructs like non-nullable structs, 'nameof()' and 'new' expressions are known to never be null, so 'ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull' will never throw.

rules.title: Do not compare Span<T> to 'null' or 'default'
rules.desc: Comparing a span to 'null' or 'default' might not do what you intended. 'default' and the 'null' literal are implicitly converted to 'Span<T>.Empty'. Remove the redundant comparison or make the code more explicit by using 'IsEmpty'.

rules.title: File-based program entry point should start with '#!'
rules.desc: When a file-based program consists of multiple files, the entry point file should start with a shebang ('#!') line to clearly distinguish it from other included files.

rules.title: Do not use insecure deserializer BinaryFormatter
rules.desc: The method '{0}' is insecure when deserializing untrusted data.  If you need to instead detect BinaryFormatter deserialization without a SerializationBinder set, then disable rule CA2300, and enable rules CA2301 and CA2302.

rules.title: Do not call BinaryFormatter.Deserialize without first setting BinaryFormatter.Binder
Ensure BinaryFormatter.Binder is set before calling BinaryFormatter.Deserialize
Do not use insecure deserializer LosFormatter
Do not use insecure deserializer NetDataContractSerializer
rules.desc: The method '{0}' is insecure when deserializing untrusted data.  If you need to instead detect NetDataContractSerializer deserialization without a SerializationBinder set, then disable rule CA2310, and enable rules CA2311 and CA2312.

rules.title: Do not deserialize without first setting NetDataContractSerializer.Binder
Ensure NetDataContractSerializer.Binder is set before deserializing
Do not use insecure deserializer ObjectStateFormatter
Do not deserialize with JavaScriptSerializer using a SimpleTypeResolver
Ensure JavaScriptSerializer is not initialized with SimpleTypeResolver before deserializing
Do not use TypeNameHandling values other than None
rules.desc: Deserializing JSON when using a TypeNameHandling value other than None can be insecure.  If you need to instead detect Json.NET deserialization when a SerializationBinder isn't specified, then disable rule CA2326, and enable rules CA2327, CA2328, CA2329, and CA2330.

rules.title: Do not use insecure JsonSerializerSettings
Ensure that JsonSerializerSettings are secure
Do not deserialize with JsonSerializer using an insecure configuration
Ensure that JsonSerializer has a secure configuration when deserializing
Do not use DataTable.ReadXml() with untrusted data
Do not use DataSet.ReadXml() with untrusted data
Unsafe DataSet or DataTable in serializable type can be vulnerable to remote code execution attacks
Unsafe DataSet or DataTable in serializable type
Unsafe DataSet or DataTable in deserialized object graph can be vulnerable to remote code execution attacks
Unsafe DataSet or DataTable type found in deserializable object graph
Unsafe DataSet or DataTable type in web deserializable object graph
Ensure auto-generated class containing DataSet.ReadXml() is not used with untrusted data
Unsafe DataSet or DataTable in auto-generated serializable type can be vulnerable to remote code execution attacks
Review code for SQL injection vulnerabilities
Review code for XSS vulnerabilities
Review code for file path injection vulnerabilities
Review code for information disclosure vulnerabilities
Review code for LDAP injection vulnerabilities
Review code for process command injection vulnerabilities
Review code for open redirect vulnerabilities
Review code for XPath injection vulnerabilities
Review code for XML injection vulnerabilities
Review code for XAML injection vulnerabilities
Review code for DLL injection vulnerabilities
Review code for regex injection vulnerabilities
Do Not Add Schema By URL
rules.desc: This overload of XmlSchemaCollection.Add method internally enables DTD processing on the XML reader instance used, and uses UrlResolver for resolving external XML entities. The outcome is information disclosure. Content from file system or network shares for the machine processing the XML can be exposed to attacker. In addition, an attacker can use this as a DoS vector.

rules.title: Insecure DTD processing in XML
rules.desc: Using XmlTextReader.Load(), creating an insecure XmlReaderSettings instance when invoking XmlReader.Create(), setting the InnerXml property of the XmlDocument and enabling DTD processing using XmlUrlResolver insecurely can lead to information disclosure. Replace it with a call to the Load() method overload that takes an XmlReader instance, use XmlReader.Create() to accept XmlReaderSettings arguments or consider explicitly setting secure values. The DataViewSettingCollectionString property of DataViewManager should always be assigned from a trusted source, the DtdProcessing property should be set to false, and the XmlResolver property should be changed to XmlSecureResolver or null.

rules.title: Insecure XSLT script processing
rules.desc: Providing an insecure XsltSettings instance and an insecure XmlResolver instance to XslCompiledTransform.Load method is potentially unsafe as it allows processing script within XSL, which on an untrusted XSL input may lead to malicious code execution. Either replace the insecure XsltSettings argument with XsltSettings.Default or an instance that has disabled document function and script execution, or replace the XmlResolver argument with null or an XmlSecureResolver instance. This message may be suppressed if the input is known to be from a trusted source and external resource resolution from locations that are not known in advance must be supported.

rules.title: Insecure Processing in API Design, XmlDocument and XmlTextReader
rules.desc: Enabling DTD processing on all instances derived from XmlTextReader or  XmlDocument and using XmlUrlResolver for resolving external XML entities may lead to information disclosure. Ensure to set the XmlResolver property to null, create an instance of XmlSecureResolver when processing untrusted input, or use XmlReader.Create method with a secure XmlReaderSettings argument. Unless you need to enable it, ensure the DtdProcessing property is set to false.

rules.title: Mark Verb Handlers With Validate Antiforgery Token
Do Not Use Weak Cryptographic Algorithms
rules.desc: Cryptographic algorithms degrade over time as attacks become for advances to attacker get access to more computation. Depending on the type and application of this cryptographic algorithm, further degradation of the cryptographic strength of it may allow attackers to read enciphered messages, tamper with enciphered  messages, forge digital signatures, tamper with hashed content, or otherwise compromise any cryptosystem based on this algorithm. Replace encryption uses with the AES algorithm (AES-256, AES-192 and AES-128 are acceptable) with a key length greater than or equal to 128 bits. Replace hashing uses with a hashing function in the SHA-2 family, such as SHA-2 512, SHA-2 384, or SHA-2 256.

rules.title: Do Not Use Broken Cryptographic Algorithms
rules.desc: An attack making it computationally feasible to break this algorithm exists. This allows attackers to break the cryptographic guarantees it is designed to provide. Depending on the type and application of this cryptographic algorithm, this may allow attackers to read enciphered messages, tamper with enciphered  messages, forge digital signatures, tamper with hashed content, or otherwise compromise any cryptosystem based on this algorithm. Replace encryption uses with the AES algorithm (AES-256, AES-192 and AES-128 are acceptable) with a key length greater than or equal to 128 bits. Replace hashing uses with a hashing function in the SHA-2 family, such as SHA512, SHA384, or SHA256. Replace digital signature uses with RSA with a key length greater than or equal to 2048-bits, or ECDSA with a key length greater than or equal to 256 bits.

rules.title: Review cipher mode usage with cryptography experts
rules.desc: These cipher modes might be vulnerable to attacks. Consider using recommended modes (CBC, CTS).

rules.title: Do Not Disable Certificate Validation
rules.desc: A certificate can help authenticate the identity of the server. Clients should validate the server certificate to ensure requests are sent to the intended server. If the ServerCertificateValidationCallback always returns 'true', any certificate will pass validation.

rules.title: Do Not Call Dangerous Methods In Deserialization
rules.desc: Insecure Deserialization is a vulnerability which occurs when untrusted data is used to abuse the logic of an application, inflict a Denial-of-Service (DoS) attack, or even execute arbitrary code upon it being deserialized. It’s frequently possible for malicious users to abuse these deserialization features when the application is deserializing untrusted data which is under their control. Specifically, invoke dangerous methods in the process of deserialization. Successful insecure deserialization attacks could allow an attacker to carry out attacks such as DoS attacks, authentication bypasses, and remote code execution.

rules.title: Do Not Disable SChannel Use of Strong Crypto
rules.desc: Starting with the .NET Framework 4.6, the System.Net.ServicePointManager and System.Net.Security.SslStream classes are recommended to use new protocols. The old ones have protocol weaknesses and are not supported. Setting Switch.System.Net.DontEnableSchUseStrongCrypto with true will use the old weak crypto check and opt out of the protocol migration.

rules.title: Potential reference cycle in deserialized object graph
rules.desc: Review code that processes untrusted deserialized data for handling of unexpected reference cycles. An unexpected reference cycle should not cause the code to enter an infinite loop. Otherwise, an unexpected reference cycle can allow an attacker to DOS or exhaust the memory of the process when deserializing untrusted data.

rules.title: Do Not Disable Request Validation
rules.desc: Request validation is a feature in ASP.NET that examines HTTP requests and determines whether they contain potentially dangerous content. This check adds protection from markup or code in the URL query string, cookies, or posted form values that might have been added for malicious purposes. So, it is generally desirable and should be left enabled for defense in depth.

rules.title: Do Not Use Deprecated Security Protocols
rules.desc: Using a deprecated security protocol rather than the system default is risky.

rules.title: Do Not Disable HTTP Header Checking
rules.desc: HTTP header checking enables encoding of the carriage return and newline characters, \r and \n, that are found in response headers. This encoding can help to avoid injection attacks that exploit an application that echoes untrusted data contained by the header.

rules.title: Use XmlReader for 'DataSet.ReadXml()'
rules.desc: Processing XML from untrusted data may load dangerous external references, which should be restricted by using an XmlReader with a secure resolver or with DTD processing disabled.

rules.title: Do Not Serialize Types With Pointer Fields
rules.desc: Pointers are not "type safe" in the sense that you cannot guarantee the correctness of the memory they point at. So, serializing types with pointer fields is dangerous, as it may allow an attacker to control the pointer.

rules.title: Set ViewStateUserKey For Classes Derived From Page
rules.desc: Setting the ViewStateUserKey property can help you prevent attacks on your application by allowing you to assign an identifier to the view-state variable for individual users so that they cannot use the variable to generate an attack. Otherwise, there will be cross-site request forgery vulnerabilities.

rules.title: Use XmlReader for 'XmlSerializer.Deserialize()'
rules.desc: Processing XML from untrusted data may load dangerous external references, which should be restricted by using an XmlReader with a secure resolver or with DTD processing disabled.

rules.title: Use XmlReader for XmlValidatingReader constructor
rules.desc: Processing XML from untrusted data may load dangerous external references, which should be restricted by using an XmlReader with a secure resolver or with DTD processing disabled.

rules.title: Use XmlReader for 'XmlSchema.Read()'
rules.desc: Processing XML from untrusted data may load dangerous external references, which should be restricted by using an XmlReader with a secure resolver or with DTD processing disabled.

rules.title: Use XmlReader for XPathDocument constructor
rules.desc: Processing XML from untrusted data may load dangerous external references, which should be restricted by using an XmlReader with a secure resolver or with DTD processing disabled.

rules.title: Do not use obsolete key derivation function
rules.desc: Password-based key derivation should use PBKDF2 with SHA-2. Avoid using PasswordDeriveBytes since it generates a PBKDF1 key. Avoid using Rfc2898DeriveBytes.CryptDeriveKey since it doesn't use the iteration count or salt.

rules.title: Do Not Use XslTransform
Do Not Use Account Shared Access Signature
rules.desc: Shared Access Signatures(SAS) are a vital part of the security model for any application using Azure Storage, they should provide limited and safe permissions to your storage account to clients that don't have the account key. All of the operations available via a service SAS are also available via an account SAS, that is, account SAS is too powerful. So it is recommended to use Service SAS to delegate access more carefully.

rules.title: Use SharedAccessProtocol HttpsOnly
rules.desc: HTTPS encrypts network traffic. Use HttpsOnly, rather than HttpOrHttps, to ensure network traffic is always encrypted to help prevent disclosure of sensitive data.

rules.title: Use Container Level Access Policy
rules.desc: No access policy identifier is specified, making tokens non-revocable.

rules.title: Do not disable ServicePointManagerSecurityProtocols
Ensure Key Derivation Function algorithm is sufficiently strong
rules.desc: Some implementations of the Rfc2898DeriveBytes class allow for a hash algorithm to be specified in a constructor parameter or overwritten in the HashAlgorithm property. If a hash algorithm is specified, then it should be SHA-256 or higher.

rules.title: Do Not Add Certificates To Root Store
rules.desc: By default, the Trusted Root Certification Authorities certificate store is configured with a set of public CAs that has met the requirements of the Microsoft Root Certificate Program. Since all trusted root CAs can issue certificates for any domain, an attacker can pick a weak or coercible CA that you install by yourself to target for an attack - and a single vulnerable, malicious or coercible CA undermines the security of the entire system. To make matters worse, these attacks can go unnoticed quite easily.

rules.title: Ensure Certificates Are Not Added To Root Store
rules.desc: By default, the Trusted Root Certification Authorities certificate store is configured with a set of public CAs that has met the requirements of the Microsoft Root Certificate Program. Since all trusted root CAs can issue certificates for any domain, an attacker can pick a weak or coercible CA that you install by yourself to target for an attack - and a single vulnerable, malicious or coercible CA undermines the security of the entire system. To make matters worse, these attacks can go unnoticed quite easily.

rules.title: Use Secure Cookies In ASP.NET Core
rules.desc: Applications available over HTTPS must use secure cookies.

rules.title: Ensure Use Secure Cookies In ASP.NET Core
rules.desc: Applications available over HTTPS must use secure cookies.

rules.title: Do Not Use Digital Signature Algorithm (DSA)
rules.desc: DSA is too weak to use.

rules.title: Use Rivest-Shamir-Adleman (RSA) Algorithm With Sufficient Key Size
rules.desc: Encryption algorithms are vulnerable to brute force attacks when too small a key size is used.

rules.title: Avoid hardcoding SecurityProtocolType value
Do Not Use Weak Key Derivation Function With Insufficient Iteration Count
rules.desc: When deriving cryptographic keys from user-provided inputs such as password, use sufficient iteration count (at least 100k).

rules.title: Ensure Sufficient Iteration Count When Using Weak Key Derivation Function
rules.desc: When deriving cryptographic keys from user-provided inputs such as password, use sufficient iteration count (at least 100k).

rules.title: Do Not Add Archive Item's Path To The Target File System Path
rules.desc: When extracting files from an archive and using the archive item's path, check if the path is safe. Archive path can be relative and can lead to file system access outside of the expected file system target path, leading to malicious config changes and remote code execution via lay-and-wait technique.

rules.title: Do not hard-code encryption key
rules.desc: SymmetricAlgorithm's .Key property, or a method's rgbKey parameter, should never be a hard-coded value.

rules.title: Use antiforgery tokens in ASP.NET Core MVC controllers
rules.desc: Handling a POST, PUT, PATCH, or DELETE request without validating an antiforgery token may be vulnerable to cross-site request forgery attacks. A cross-site request forgery attack can send malicious requests from an authenticated user to your ASP.NET Core MVC controller.

rules.title: Use DefaultDllImportSearchPaths attribute for P/Invokes
rules.desc: By default, P/Invokes using DllImportAttribute probe a number of directories, including the current working directory for the library to load. This can be a security issue for certain applications, leading to DLL hijacking.

rules.title: Do not use unsafe DllImportSearchPath value
rules.desc: There could be a malicious DLL in the default DLL search directories. Or, depending on where your application is run from, there could be a malicious DLL in the application's directory. Use a DllImportSearchPath value that specifies an explicit search path instead. The DllImportSearchPath flags that this rule looks for can be configured in .editorconfig.

rules.title: Do not use insecure randomness
rules.desc: Using a cryptographically weak pseudo-random number generator may allow an attacker to predict what security-sensitive value will be generated. Use a cryptographically strong random number generator if an unpredictable value is required, or ensure that weak pseudo-random numbers aren't used in a security-sensitive manner.

rules.title: Miss HttpVerb attribute for action methods
rules.desc: All the methods that create, edit, delete, or otherwise modify data do so in the [HttpPost] overload of the method, which needs to be protected with the anti forgery attribute from request forgery. Performing a GET operation should be a safe operation that has no side effects and doesn't modify your persisted data.

rules.title: Set HttpOnly to true for HttpCookie
rules.desc: As a defense in depth measure, ensure security sensitive HTTP cookies are marked as HttpOnly. This indicates web browsers should disallow scripts from accessing the cookies. Injected malicious scripts are a common way of stealing cookies.

rules.title: Do not use deprecated SslProtocols values
rules.desc: Older protocol versions of Transport Layer Security (TLS) are less secure than TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3, and are more likely to have new vulnerabilities. Avoid older protocol versions to minimize risk.

rules.title: Avoid hardcoded SslProtocols values
rules.desc: Current Transport Layer Security protocol versions may become deprecated if vulnerabilities are found. Avoid hardcoding SslProtocols values to keep your application secure. Use 'None' to let the Operating System choose a version.

rules.title: HttpClients should enable certificate revocation list checks
rules.desc: Using HttpClient without providing a platform specific handler (WinHttpHandler or CurlHandler or HttpClientHandler) where the CheckCertificateRevocationList property is set to true, will allow revoked certificates to be accepted by the HttpClient as valid.

rules.title: Ensure HttpClient certificate revocation list check is not disabled
rules.desc: Using HttpClient without providing a platform specific handler (WinHttpHandler or CurlHandler or HttpClientHandler) where the CheckCertificateRevocationList property is set to true, will allow revoked certificates to be accepted by the HttpClient as valid.

rules.title: Do not use CreateEncryptor with non-default IV
rules.desc: Symmetric encryption should always use a non-repeatable initialization vector to prevent dictionary attacks.

rules.title: Use CreateEncryptor with the default IV
rules.desc: Symmetric encryption should always use a non-repeatable initialization vector to prevent dictionary attacks.

rules.title: Do not hard-code certificate
rules.desc: Hard-coded certificates in source code are vulnerable to being exploited.

rules.title: Do not disable token validation checks
rules.desc: Token validation checks ensure that while validating tokens, all aspects are analyzed and verified. Turning off validation can lead to security holes by allowing untrusted tokens to make it through validation.

rules.title: Do not always skip token validation in delegates
rules.desc: By setting critical TokenValidationParameter validation delegates to true, important authentication safeguards are disabled which can lead to tokens from any issuer or expired tokens being wrongly validated.

Add the following PropertyGroup to your MSBuild project file to enable IDE0005 (Remove unnecessary usings/imports) on build:
  <PropertyGroup>
    <!--
      Make sure any documentation comments which are included in code get checked for syntax during the build, but do
      not report warnings for missing comments.
      CS1573: Parameter 'parameter' has no matching param tag in the XML comment for 'parameter' (but other parameters do)
      CS1591: Missing XML comment for publicly visible type or member 'Type_or_Member'
      CS1712: Type parameter 'type_parameter' has no matching typeparam tag in the XML comment on 'type_or_member' (but other type parameters do)
    -->
    <GenerateDocumentationFile>True</GenerateDocumentationFile>
    <NoWarn>$(NoWarn),1573,1591,1712</NoWarn>
  </PropertyGroup>

rules.title: Accessors should be ordered

rules.title: Avoid Task.Result
rules.desc: To avoid deadlocks, methods may not call Result on a Task.

rules.title: Do not use spaces in file names.

rules.title: Path too long, make smaller to avoid $MAX_RELATIVE_PATH_LENGTH limit.
rules.desc: Too long path.

rules.desc: Assignment in condition.

rules.title: Log caught exceptions setup
rules.desc: This analyzer requires additional configuration in the .editorconfig or <AdditionalFiles> element.

rules.title: Use inner exceptions for unhandled exceptions
rules.desc: Use inner exceptions for unhandled exceptions

rules.title: Limit the number of clauses in a condition
rules.desc: Limit the number of clauses in a condition

rules.title: Prefer tuples that have names
rules.desc: Name this tuple field for readability

rules.title: Prefer tuple field names over generic item1, item2, etc
rules.desc: For readability use the name provided for this field, not a generic field name

rules.title: Avoid async void
rules.desc: To avoid unhandled exception, methods should not use async void unless a event handler.

rules.title: Avoid empty statement blocks
rules.desc: Avoid empty statement blocks

rules.title: Avoid empty catch blocks
rules.desc: Avoid empty catch blocks

rules.title: Ensure FileVersion is the same as PackageVersion
rules.desc: Ensure FileVersion is the same as PackageVersion

rules.title: Dereference Null after As

rules.title: Documentation text should add value
rules.desc: Summary XML comments for classes, methods, etc. must add more information then just repeating its name.

rules.title: Avoid method calls as arguments
rules.desc: Avoid method calls as arguments to method calls

rules.title: Put every linq statement on a separate line
rules.desc: Put every linq statement on a separate line

rules.title: Align number of + and - operators.
rules.desc: Overload the - operator, when you overload the + operator, as they are often used in combination with each other.

rules.title: Align number of * and / operators.
rules.desc: Overload the / operator, when you overload the * operator, as they are often used in combination with each other.

rules.title: Align number of > and < operators.
rules.desc: Overload the < operator, when you overload the > operator, as they are often used in combination with each other.

rules.title: Align number of >= and <= operators.
rules.desc: Overload the <= operator, when you overload the >= operator, as they are often used in combination with each other.

rules.title: Align number of >> and << operators.
rules.desc: Overload the << operator, when you overload the >> operator, as they are often used in combination with each other.

rules.title: Align number of ++ and -- operators.
rules.desc: Overload the -- operator, when you overload the ++ operator, as they are often used in combination with each other.

rules.title: Reduce Cognitive Load
rules.desc: This method has too many nested block statements and logical cases to consider in this method

rules.title: Avoid overriding methods or properties with the new keyword.
rules.desc: Overriding with the new keyword gives unexpected behavior for the callers of the overridden method or property.

rules.title: Merge If Statements
rules.desc: Merging If statement with outer If statement to reduce cognitive load

rules.title: Avoid empty statements
rules.desc: Avoid empty statements

rules.title: Avoid putting multiple Lambda expressions on the same line
rules.desc: Avoid putting multiple Lambda expressions on the same line. To improve readability, split them into separate lines.

rules.title: Don't use ArrayList, use List<T> instead
rules.desc: Usage of Arraylist is discouraged by Microsoft for performance reasons, use List<T> instead.

rules.title: Avoid unnecessary 'Where'
rules.desc: Invoking Where is unnecessary

rules.title: Avoid inline magic numbers
rules.desc: Avoid inline magic number, define them as constant or include in an enumeration instead.

rules.title: Cast the complete object
rules.desc: A cast should include all information from the previous type. By casting to a type of one of the fields, the cast is losing information. Use an AsType() or ToType() method instead.

rules.title: Document thrown exceptions
rules.desc: Be clear to your callers what exception can be thrown from your method by mentioning each of them in an <exception> element in the documentation of the method.

rules.title: Throw only informational exceptions
rules.desc: Specify context to a thrown exception, by using a constructor overload that sets the Message property.

rules.title: Avoid throwing exceptions from unexpected locations
rules.desc: Avoid throwing exceptions from unexpected locations, like Finalizers, Dispose, Static Constructors, etc...

rules.title: Pass sender to event handler
rules.desc: Prevent passing null values for sender/object to event handler (for instance-based events).

rules.title: Document unhandled exceptions
rules.desc: Be clear to your callers what exception can be thrown from your method (or any called methods) by mentioning each of them in an <exception> element in the documentation of the method.

rules.title: Align number of + and == operators.
rules.desc: Overload the == operator, when you overload the + operator, as they are often used in combination with each other.

rules.title: Don't use parameters as temporary variables
rules.desc: Don't use parameters as temporary variables, define a local variable instead.

rules.title: Don't change loop variables
rules.desc: Don't change loop variables, this gives unexpected loop iterations. Use continue and break instead.

rules.title: Avoid multiple conditions on the same line.
rules.desc: Avoid multiple conditions on the same line of a multi-line condition statement. Instead, break lines right after the logical operators.

rules.title: Return only immutable collections
rules.desc: Return only immutable or readonly collections from a public method, otherwise these collections can be changed by the caller without the callee noticing.

rules.title: Avoid implementing a finalizer
rules.desc: Avoid implement a finalizer, use Dispose instead. If the class has unmanaged fields, finalizers are allowed if they only call Dispose.

rules.title: Align filename and class name
rules.desc: Name the file after the class, struct or enum it contains

rules.title: Remove commented code
rules.desc: Remove commented code

rules.title: Unmanaged object need disposing
rules.desc: Every field which holds an unmanaged object needs to be declared in a class that implements IDisposable.

rules.title: Set properties in any order
rules.desc: Getting other properties in a setter makes this setter dependent on the order in which these properties are set.

rules.title: Namespace matches Assembly Name
rules.desc: In order to prevent pollution of namespaces, and maintainability of namespaces, the Assembly Name and Namespace must match.

rules.title: Avoid Duplicate Strings
rules.desc: Duplicate strings are less maintainable

rules.title: Method returns void
rules.desc: Void returns imply a hidden side effect, since there is otherwise a singularly unique unit function.

rules.title: Enable documentation creation
rules.desc: Enable documentation creation

rules.title: Avoid the ExcludeFromCodeCoverage attribute
rules.desc: Avoid the ExcludeFromCodeCoverage attribute

rules.title: Avoid empty regions
rules.desc: Remove the empty region

rules.title: Avoid casting to string
rules.desc: Avoid casting to string, use `ToString()` or a serialization solution

rules.title: Don't use Assembly.GetEntryAssembly()
rules.desc: During testing Assembly.GetEntryAssembly will point to the test runner, which is not expected.

rules.title: Backwards for-loop boundary check should use >= 0 instead of > 0
rules.desc: When looping backwards from a collection count to 0, use '>= 0' to ensure the element at index 0 is processed

rules.title: Avoid string.Format in interpolated string
rules.desc: Using string.Format within interpolated strings can be simplified by using direct interpolation

rules.title: Avoid calling ToString() on string type
rules.desc: Calling ToString() on an expression that is already of type string is redundant and should be removed.

rules.title: Avoid variables named exactly '_'
rules.desc: Variables named exactly '_' can be confused with C# discards. Use either a proper discard or a more descriptive variable name.

rules.title: Avoid problematic using statement patterns
rules.desc: Avoid using statements with fields or variables.

rules.title: Avoid TODO comments
rules.desc: Source code is not the place to get attention for a workitem. Use a proper task management system instead.

rules.title: Avoid calling ToString() when the result is discarded
rules.desc: Calling ToString() when the result is assigned to a discard variable or used as a standalone expression statement is unnecessary and should be removed.

rules.title: Avoid unnecessary parentheses in attributes
rules.desc: Attributes without arguments should not have empty parentheses. For example: [TestClass()] => [TestClass]

rules.title: Mock<T> construction must call an existing constructor
rules.desc: Could not find a constructor that matched the given arguments

rules.title: Mock<T>.Raise(x => x.Event += null, sender, args) must have correct parameters
rules.desc: Parameter mismatch

rules.title: Mock<T>.Raise(x => x.Event += null, sender, args) must have correct parameters
rules.desc: Parameter mismatch

rules.title: Mock<T> of disposable concrete class should setup virtual Dispose(bool)
rules.desc: Mocking a disposable concrete class without configuring protected Dispose may prevent cleanup from executing

rules.title: Test Method names unhelpful prefix
rules.desc: Test Method names must not start with 'Test', 'Ensure', or 'Verify'. Otherwise, they are more difficult to find in sorted lists in Test Explorer.

rules.title: Assert.AreEqual/AreNotEqual Usage
rules.desc: Assert.AreEqual(<actual>, <expected>) => Assert.AreEqual(<expected>, <actual>) and Assert.AreEqual(null, <actual>) => Assert.IsNull(<actual>).

rules.title: Avoid ExpectedException attribute
rules.desc: The [ExpectedException()] attribute does not have line number granularity and trips the debugger anyway.  Use AssertEx.Throws() instead.

rules.title: TestContext Usage
rules.desc: TestContext should not be included in test classes unless it is actually used.

rules.title: Assert.AreEqual parameter types must match
rules.desc: The types of the parameters of Are[Not]Equal must match.

rules.title: Assert.IsTrue/IsFalse Usage
rules.desc: Assert.IsTrue(<actual> == <expected>) => Assert.AreEqual(<expected>, <actual>)

rules.title: Assert.IsTrue/IsFalse Should not be in parenthesis
rules.desc: Assert.IsTrue((<actual> == <expected>)) => Assert.IsTrue(<expected> == <actual>)

rules.title: Test must have proper Description Attribute value
rules.desc: Test Description Attribute must not have a literal string and length of the reference value should be less than 25 characters.

rules.title: Test must have an appropriate Timeout
rules.desc: Tests that lack a Timeout may indefinitely block.

rules.title: Ignore attribute not allowed
rules.desc: The Ignore attribute creates dead code and build warnings.  Rather than ignoring a test, fix it or remove it.  (Rely on Version Control to save it.)

rules.title: Owner attribute not allowed
rules.desc: The Owner attribute is no more relevant.

rules.title: Test must have an appropriate TestCategory
rules.desc: Tests are required to have an appropriate TestCategory to allow running tests category wise.

rules.title: TestInitialize methods not allowed
rules.desc: TestInitialize methods are not deterministic and can create unexpected test results.

rules.title: ClassInitialize methods not allowed
rules.desc: ClassInitialize methods are not deterministic and can create unexpected test results.

rules.title: ClassCleanup methods not allowed
rules.desc: ClassCleanup methods are not deterministic and can create unexpected test results.

rules.title: TestCleanup methods not allowed
rules.desc: TestCleanup methods are not deterministic and can create unexpected test results.

rules.title: SuppressMessage not allowed
rules.desc: SuppressMessage results in violations of codified coding guidelines.

rules.title: DataTestMethods must have at least 1 DataRow or 1 DynamicData, TestMethods must have none
rules.desc: DataTestMethods are only executed with DataRows

rules.title: TestMethods/DataTestMethods must be in [TestClass]
rules.desc: Tests are only executed if they are [TestClass]

rules.title: TestMethods/DataTestMethods must have the correct number of arguments
rules.desc: DataTestMethods should have the same number of parameters of the DataRows, TestMethods should have no arguments

rules.title: TestMethods/DataTestMethods must be public, instance methods
TestMethods/DataTestMethods should not have the same name
[TestClass] must be a public instance class
Avoid MS Fakes
rules.desc: Avoid MS Fakes. Use Moq instead for example.  If applicable, remove the Reference and the .fakes file as well.

rules.title: No Test Methods
rules.desc: Remove empty test method '{0}'

rules.title: Assert.IsTrue(true) Usage
rules.desc: Do not call IsTrue/IsFalse with a literal true/false

rules.title: Assert.AreEqual(true, true) Usage
rules.desc: Do not call AreEqual with a literal true/false

rules.title: Assert Inline Null Check Usage
rules.desc: Assert.AreEqual(<actual>?.attribute, <expected>) => Assert.IsNotNull(<actual>); Assert.AreEqual(<actual>.attribute, <expected>)

rules.title: Test class public method should be a Test method
rules.desc: Test class cannot have a public method unless its a test method. Either change the access modifier or make it a test method

rules.title: Assert.Fail should not be used if an alternative is more appropriate
TestMethods must return void or Task for async methods
rules.desc: MSTest will not run tests that return something other than void, or Task for async tests.

rules.title: Use a testable Time Provider
rules.desc: For testability, the behavior of time providers should be adjustable under test. DateTime.Now, DateTime.UtcNow, and DateTime.Today lack this possibility.

rules.title: Parse should not fail
rules.desc: Parsing string literals should not fail, as it will crash at runtime.

rules.title: Decorate pure functions
rules.desc: To help the compiler and code analyzers determine the proper usage of pure functions.

rules.title: Characters with Trojan Horse potential are not allowed
rules.desc: When characters with Trojan Horse potential are found, they should be blocked to avoid security risks to the application.

rules.title: Seal concrete classes unless designed for inheritance
rules.desc: Inheritance is one of the pillars of Object Oriented Programming. Designing a class to support inheritance however, is hard. As a consequence, it is considered a bad practice to unintentionally allowing a class to be inheritable.

rules.title: Only unsealed concrete classes should be decorated as inheritable
rules.desc: The inheritable attribute is only meant to be used on concrete classes.

rules.title: Use file-scoped namespace declarations
rules.desc: It reduces the number of braces in a file, and also eliminates the wasted horizontal space to the left of the class definition, since it no longer needs to be indented.

rules.title: Define properties as not-nullable for types with a defined empty state
rules.desc: Value types with an empty state do not benefit from adding nullability to it, because the nullable that has a value can still represent an empty state.

rules.title: Define properties as not-nullable for enums with a defined none/empty value
rules.desc: Enums with a none value do not benefit from adding nullability to it, because the nullable that has a value can still represent an none/empty state.

rules.title: Use System.DateOnly instead of Qowaiv.Date
rules.desc: The purpose of `Qowaiv.Date` is to provide a date (only) alternative to DateTime. Since .NET 6.0, Microsoft provides DateOnly.

rules.title: Define properties as immutables
rules.desc: Immutable types (classes, interfaces, records, structs) have multiple advantages. To benefit from this, all properties should be defined as immutable.

rules.title: Use immutable types for properties
rules.desc: Immutable types (classes, interfaces, records, structs) have multiple advantages. To benefit from this, the type of properties should be immutable.

rules.title: Use Qowaiv decimal rounding
rules.desc: Both the extended functionality and the extension method are reasons to adopt Qowaiv decimal rounding.

rules.title: Define global using statements separately
rules.desc: For design and maintainability reasons, it is key that all global usings statements are grouped.

rules.title: Define global using statements in single file
rules.desc: For design and maintainability reasons, it is key that all global usings statements are grouped.

rules.title: Prefer regular over positional properties
rules.desc: The usage of positional properties, defined in a primary constructor, turns out to be cumbersome for public APIs. Therefor the use of regular properties is preferred in those cases.

rules.title: Apply arithmetic operations on non-nullables only
rules.desc: .NET allows arithmetic operations between nullable value types. The outcome will be null if any of the arguments turns out to be null, which can be confusing or a bug.

rules.title: Use Qowaiv.Clock.TimeProvider
rules.desc: The purpose of `Qowaiv.Time` is to provide a time (only) alternative to DateTime. Since .NET 6.0, Microsoft provides TimeOnly.

rules.title: Prefer XML to LINQ over DOM
rules.desc: With the introduction of LINQ (2008) Microsoft provided a new way of creating XML, using XDocument/XElement. Defacto, the use of XmlDocument/XmlElement has become obsolete since then.

rules.title: Prefer System.Text.Json over Newtonsoft.Json
rules.desc: Use System.Text.Json for JSON serialization as it is both faster, with a smaller memory footprint, and built-in in the .NET framework.

rules.title: Use leading zeros to define date constants
rules.desc: Date constants should comply to ISO 8601 to improve readability.

rules.title: Use compliant GUID literals
rules.desc: Non-compliant GUID literals will lead to runtime errors.

rules.desc: Non-compliant GUID literals will lead to runtime errors.

rules.title: Prefer single value objects over data annotations
rules.desc: To reduce primitive obsession, use single value objects instead of data annotations.

rules.title: Use compliant validation attributes
rules.desc: Validation attributes are designed to validate certain member types. When applied on other types, this is invalid, and might even crash.

Methods and properties should be named in PascalCase
rules.desc: Shared naming conventions allow teams to collaborate efficiently.

rules.title: Types should be named in PascalCase
rules.desc: Shared naming conventions allow teams to collaborate efficiently.

rules.title: Lines should not be too long
rules.desc: Scrolling horizontally to see a full line of code lowers the code readability.

rules.title: Files should not have too many lines of code
rules.desc: When a source file grows too much, it can accumulate numerous responsibilities and become challenging to understand and maintain.

rules.title: Tabulation characters should not be used
rules.desc: The tab width can differ from one development environment to another. Using tabs may require other developers to configure their environment (text editor, preferences, etc.) to read source code.

rules.title: Standard outputs should not be used directly to log anything
rules.desc: In software development, logs serve as a record of events within an application, providing crucial insights for debugging. When logging, it is essential to ensure that the logs are:

rules.title: Methods should not have too many parameters
rules.desc: Methods with a long parameter list are difficult to use because maintainers must figure out the role of each parameter and keep track of their position.

rules.title: Nested blocks of code should not be left empty
rules.desc: An empty code block is confusing. It will require some effort from maintainers to determine if it is intentional or indicates the implementation is incomplete.

rules.title: Magic numbers should not be used
rules.desc: A magic number is a hard-coded numerical value that may lack context or meaning. They should not be used because they can make the code less readable and maintainable.

rules.title: Inheritance tree of classes should not be too deep
rules.desc: Inheritance is one of the most valuable concepts in object-oriented programming. It’s a way to categorize and reuse code by creating collections of attributes and behaviors called classes, which can be based on previously created classes.

rules.title: General or reserved exceptions should never be thrown
rules.desc: This rule raises an issue when a general or reserved exception is thrown.

rules.title: Files should end with a newline
rules.desc: Some tools work better when files end with an empty line.

rules.title: Control structures should use curly braces
rules.desc: Control structures are code statements that impact the program’s control flow (e.g., if statements, for loops, etc.)

rules.title: Statements should be on separate lines
rules.desc: Putting multiple statements on a single line lowers the code readability and makes debugging the code more complex.

rules.title: Sections of code should not be commented out
rules.desc: Commented-out code distracts the focus from the actual executed code. It creates a noise that increases maintenance code. And because it is never executed, it quickly becomes out of date and invalid.

rules.title: "if ... else if" constructs should end with "else" clauses
rules.desc: This rule applies whenever an if statement is followed by one or more else if statements; the final else if should be followed by an else statement.

rules.title: "for" loop stop conditions should be invariant
rules.desc: A for loop stop condition should test the loop counter against an invariant value, one that is true at both the beginning and ending of every loop iteration. Ideally, this means that the stop condition is set to a local variable just before the loop begins.

rules.title: "switch/Select" statements should contain a "default/Case Else" clauses
rules.desc: The requirement for a final default clause is defensive programming. The clause should either take appropriate action, or contain a suitable comment as to why no action is taken. Even when the switch covers all current values of an enum, a default case should still be used because there is no guarantee that the enum won’t be extended.

rules.title: Control flow statements "if", "switch", "for", "foreach", "while", "do"  and "try" should not be nested too deeply
rules.desc: Nested control flow statements if, switch, for, foreach, while, do, and try are often key ingredients in creating what’s known as "Spaghetti code". This code smell can make your program difficult to understand and maintain.

rules.title: Functions should not have too many lines of code
rules.desc: A function that grows too large tends to aggregate too many responsibilities.

rules.title: Literal suffixes should be upper case
rules.desc: Using upper case literal suffixes removes the potential ambiguity between "1" (digit 1) and "l" (letter el) for declaring literals.

rules.title: Increment (++) and decrement (--) operators should not be used in a method call or mixed with other operators in an expression
rules.desc: The use of increment and decrement operators in method calls or in combination with other arithmetic operators is not recommended, because:

rules.title: "goto" statement should not be used
rules.desc: goto is an unstructured control flow statement. It makes code less readable and maintainable. Structured control flow statements such as if, for, while, continue or break should be used instead.

rules.title: Parameter names should match base declaration and other partial definitions
rules.desc: Parameters are part of the method signature and its identity.

rules.title: Method overrides should not change parameter defaults
rules.desc: Default arguments are determined by the static type of the object.

rules.title: Finalizers should not throw exceptions
rules.desc: The finalizers are used to perform any necessary final clean-up when the garbage collector is collecting a class instance. The programmer has no control over when the finalizer is called; the garbage collector decides when to call it.

rules.title: Mergeable "if" statements should be combined
rules.desc: Nested code - blocks of code inside blocks of code - is eventually necessary, but increases complexity. This is why keeping the code as flat as possible, by avoiding unnecessary nesting, is considered a good practice.

rules.title: Expressions should not be too complex
rules.desc: The complexity of an expression is defined by the number of &&, || and condition ? ifTrue : ifFalse operators it contains.

rules.title: URIs should not be hardcoded
rules.desc: Hard-coding a URI makes it difficult to test a program for a variety of reasons:

rules.title: Fields should not have public accessibility
rules.desc: Public fields in public classes do not respect the encapsulation principle and have three main disadvantages:

rules.title: A close curly brace should be located at the beginning of a line
rules.desc: Shared coding conventions make it possible for a team to efficiently collaborate. This rule makes it mandatory to place a close curly brace at the beginning of a line.

rules.title: Redundant pairs of parentheses should be removed
rules.desc: Parentheses can disambiguate the order of operations in complex expressions and make the code easier to understand.

rules.title: Empty statements should be removed
rules.desc: Empty statements represented by a semicolon ; are statements that do not perform any operation. They are often the result of a typo or a misunderstanding of the language syntax. It is a good practice to remove empty statements since they don’t add value and lead to confusion and errors.

rules.title: Local variables should not shadow class fields or properties
rules.desc: Shadowing occurs when a local variable has the same name as a variable, field, or property in an outer scope.

rules.title: Utility classes should not have public constructors
rules.desc: Whenever there are portions of code that are duplicated and do not depend on the state of their container class, they can be centralized inside a "utility class". A utility class is a class that only has static members, hence it should not be instantiated.

rules.title: Assignments should not be made from within sub-expressions
rules.desc: A common code smell that can hinder the clarity of source code is making assignments within sub-expressions. This practice involves assigning a value to a variable inside a larger expression, such as within a loop or a conditional statement.

rules.title: "Obsolete" attributes should include explanations
rules.desc: The Obsolete attribute can be applied with or without a message argument. Marking something Obsolete without including advice on why it’s obsolete or what to use instead will lead maintainers to waste time trying to figure those things out.

rules.title: Boolean literals should not be redundant
rules.desc: A boolean literal can be represented in two different ways: true or false. They can be combined with logical operators (!, &&, ||, ==, !=) to produce logical expressions that represent truth values. However, comparing a boolean literal to a variable or expression that evaluates to a boolean value is unnecessary and can make the code harder to read and understand. The more complex a boolean expression is, the harder it will be for developers to understand its meaning and expected behavior, and it will favour the introduction of new bugs.

rules.title: Unnecessary "using" should be removed
rules.desc: Unnecessary using directives refer to importing namespaces, types or creating aliases that are not used or referenced anywhere in the code.

rules.title: Deprecated code should be removed
rules.desc: This rule is meant to be used as a way to track code which is marked as being deprecated. Deprecated code should eventually be removed.

rules.title: Track uses of "FIXME" tags
rules.desc: FIXME tags are commonly used to mark places where a bug is suspected, but which the developer wants to deal with later.

rules.title: Track uses of "TODO" tags
rules.desc: Developers often use TODO tags to mark areas in the code where additional work or improvements are needed but are not implemented immediately. However, these TODO tags sometimes get overlooked or forgotten, leading to incomplete or unfinished code. This rule aims to identify and address unattended TODO tags to ensure a clean and maintainable codebase. This description explores why this is a problem and how it can be fixed to improve the overall code quality.

rules.title: Unused private types or members should be removed
rules.desc: This rule raises an issue when a private/internal type or member is never referenced in the code.

rules.title: Useless "if(true) {...}" and "if(false){...}" blocks should be removed
rules.desc: if statements with conditions that are always false have the effect of making blocks of code non-functional. if statements with conditions that are always true are completely redundant, and make the code less readable.

rules.title: Exit methods should not be called
rules.desc: Calling Environment.Exit(exitCode) or Application.Exit() terminates the process and returns an exit code to the operating system..

rules.title: "switch case" clauses should not have too many lines of code
rules.desc: The switch statement should be used only to clearly define some new branches in the control flow. As soon as a case clause contains too many statements this highly decreases the readability of the overall control flow statement. In such case, the content of the case clause should be extracted into a dedicated method.

rules.title: "Any()" should be used to test for emptiness
rules.desc: When you call Any(), it clearly communicates the code’s intention, which is to check if the collection is empty. Using Count() == 0 for this purpose is less direct and makes the code slightly more complex. However, there are some cases where special attention should be paid:

rules.title: Exceptions should not be thrown in finally blocks
rules.desc: If an exception is already being thrown within the try block or caught in a catch block, throwing another exception in the finally block will override the original exception. This means that the original exception’s message and stack trace will be lost, potentially making it challenging to diagnose and troubleshoot the root cause of the problem.

rules.title: Empty arrays and collections should be returned instead of null
rules.desc: Returning null or default instead of an actual collection forces the method callers to explicitly test for null, making the code more complex and less readable.

rules.title: Unused method parameters should be removed
rules.desc: A typical code smell known as unused function parameters refers to parameters declared in a function but not used anywhere within the function’s body. While this might seem harmless at first glance, it can lead to confusion and potential errors in your code. Disregarding the values passed to such parameters, the function’s behavior will be the same, but the programmer’s intention won’t be clearly expressed anymore. Therefore, removing function parameters that are not being utilized is considered best practice.

rules.title: Overriding members should do more than simply call the same member in the base class
rules.desc: Overriding a method just to call the same method from the base class without performing any other actions is useless and misleading. The only time this is justified is in sealed overriding methods, where the effect is to lock in the parent class behavior. This rule ignores overrides of Equals and GetHashCode.

rules.title: Methods should not be empty
rules.desc: An empty method is generally considered bad practice and can lead to confusion, readability, and maintenance issues. Empty methods bring no functionality and are misleading to others as they might think the method implementation fulfills a specific and identified requirement.

rules.title: String literals should not be duplicated
rules.desc: Duplicated string literals make the process of refactoring complex and error-prone, as any change would need to be propagated on all occurrences.

rules.title: Nested code blocks should not be used
rules.desc: Nested code blocks create new scopes where variables declared within are inaccessible from the outside, and their lifespan ends with the block.

rules.title: Classes should not be coupled to too many other classes
rules.desc: According to the Single Responsibility Principle, introduced by Robert C. Martin in his book "Principles of Object Oriented Design", a class should have only one responsibility:

rules.title: "Equals(Object)" and "GetHashCode()" should be overridden in pairs
rules.desc: Suppose you override Object.Equals in a type, you must also override Object.GetHashCode. If two objects are equal according to the Equals method, then calling GetHashCode on each of them must yield the same integer. If this is not the case, many collections, such as a Hashtable or a Dictionary won’t handle class instances correctly.

rules.title: "Equals" and the comparison operators should be overridden when implementing "IComparable"
rules.desc: When you implement IComparable or IComparable<T> on a class you should also override Equals(object) and overload the comparison operators (==, !=, <, <=, >, >=). That’s because the CLR cannot automatically call your CompareTo implementation from Equals(object) or from the base comparison operator implementations. Additionally, it is best practice to override GetHashCode along with Equals.

rules.title: "GC.Collect" should not be called
rules.desc: GC.Collect is a method that forces or suggests to the garbage collector to run a collection of objects in the managed heap that are no longer being used and free their memory.

rules.title: Method parameters, caught exceptions and foreach variables' initial values should not be ignored
rules.desc: While it is technically correct to assign to parameters from within method bodies, doing so before the parameter value is read is likely a bug. Instead, initial values of parameters, caught exceptions, and foreach parameters should be, if not treated as final, then at least read before reassignment.

rules.title: break statements should not be used except for switch cases
rules.desc: This rule is deprecated, and will eventually be removed.

rules.title: Floating point numbers should not be tested for equality
rules.desc: Floating point numbers in C# (and in most other programming languages) are not precise. They are a binary approximation of the actual value. This means that even if two floating point numbers appear to be equal, they might not be due to the tiny differences in their binary representation.

rules.title: A "while" loop should be used instead of a "for" loop
rules.desc: Using a for loop without its typical structure (initialization, condition, increment) can be confusing. In those cases, it is better to use a while loop as it is more readable.
